headline: Pakistan reports eighth polio case
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has reported its eighth polio case of 2026, involving a 13-month-old girl from Khyber district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has reported its eighth polio case of 2026, involving a 13-month-old girl from Khyber district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), the affected child belongs to Union Council Janbaz-B in Tehsil Bara. This is the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year and the sixth from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, highlighting the continued threat of poliovirus transmission in the province. Although overall wild poliovirus transmission has declined in Pakistan this year, positive environmental samples from the Peshawar block, comprising Peshawar and Khyber districts, indicate continued virus circulation and a risk to unvaccinated children. The Pakistan Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) has launched a comprehensive investigation into the latest case and is assessing science-based measures to prevent further transmission, including targeted vaccination activities and strengthening routine immunisation. Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns so far in 2026, protecting more than 45 million children multiple times. Additional targeted campaigns have also been carried out in high-risk areas, including the Peshawar block, using oral and injectable vaccines. During the September subnational campaign, more than 29.3 million children were vaccinated across the country. The next campaign, scheduled for November 2 to 8, aims to protect nearly 24 million children in 97 districts, including Khyber. According to the PEI, Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8 percent, from an estimated 20,000 cases in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025. However, eight cases have been reported so far in 2026, including six from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, four of them from southern districts, and two from Sindh. Polio is a highly contagious viral disease that has no cure and can cause permanent paralysis and, in severe cases, death. However, it is preventable through safe and effective vaccination, which has been used in 195 countries, including Muslim-majority nations. The PEI has urged parents and caregivers to ensure that every child under five receives oral polio vaccine during every campaign, alongside completing routine immunisation schedules. It urged parents to ensure vaccination of all children under five during the upcoming nationwide subnational campaign scheduled for November 2 to 8. It emphasized that frontline vaccination workers continued to visit households to administer vaccines, while parents and caregivers remained essential partners in protecting children against the potentially crippling disease. Communities, religious leaders and the media have been asked to play an active role in promoting vaccination, countering misinformation and ensuring that no child was missed during the upcoming campaign. The PEI stressed that polio eradication was a collective responsibility, calling for sustained public cooperation to protect children and achieve a polio-free Pakistan.

headline: ABHI Microfinance Bank plans to raise Rs2-3b through IPO
description: LAHORE - ABHI Microfinance Bank plans to raise between Rs2 billion and Rs3 billion through an initial public offering (IPO) of 132 million ordinary shares on
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - ABHI Microfinance Bank plans to raise between Rs2 billion and Rs3 billion through an initial public offering (IPO) of 132 million ordinary shares on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), with a floor price of Rs15 per share. According to details disclosed to the PSX, the book-building process will take place on November 5 and 6, while the retail subscription period is scheduled for November 12 and 13. The book-building portion comprises 99 million ordinary shares, representing 75% of the total issue, at a floor price of Rs15 per share, including a premium of Rs5 per share. The price band allows a maximum increase of 50%, taking the upper price limit to Rs22.50 per share.

The general public portion of the offering will be fully underwritten by Arif Habib Limited, Topline Securities Limited, Growth Securities (Private) Limited and Dawood Equities Limited. At the floor price, the bank expects to raise gross proceeds of Rs1.98 billion, which will primarily be used to expand its loan portfolio and strengthen its capital base. The proposed equity injection is expected to improve the bank’s capital adequacy ratio (CAR), support balance-sheet growth and help it meet the minimum regulatory capital requirements prescribed by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) for microfinance banks.

According to the bank’s projections, the IPO proceeds will help address its capital shortfall and bring its CAR closer to the regulatory threshold. The bank’s projected profitability over the following two years is expected to further strengthen its capital position and support compliance with regulatory requirements. The bank has continued to report profits in 2026 as the management estimates a profit of approximately Rs1.5 billion in the second half of calendar year 2026, taking the projected full-year profit to around Rs3 billion. The bank’s forecast puts its 2026 profit at Rs2.927 billion. The bank expects its CAR to turn positive and reach approximately 4.3% by the end of 2026, following the addition of IPO proceeds and projected earnings, before accounting for other capital adjustments. Profitability is projected to improve further in 2027, adding to retained earnings.

headline: CDA appoints 3 retired military officers as DGs

headline: Serena Hotels celebrates 5 years of Mehfil-e-Sukhan
description: ISLAMABAD - Serena Hotels hosted the fifth edition of Mehfil-e-Sukhan on Saturday evening, bringing together some of Pakistan’s most distinguished
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Serena Hotels hosted the fifth edition of Mehfil-e-Sukhan on Saturday evening, bringing together some of Pakistan’s most distinguished poets for its annual mushaira at the Islamabad Serena Hotel. Held under Serena’s Cultural Diplomacy Initiative, the evening honoured one of the region’s oldest literary traditions, and the enduring power of Urdu verse to bring people together across generations, regions and backgrounds. Presided over by Abbas Naqvi and Shakeel Jazaib, the mehfil featured Kishwar Naheed, Iftikhar Arif, Anwar Shaoor, Abbas Tabish, Izhar ul Haq, Hamid Ateeq Sarwar, Haris Khaleeq, Ahmed Salman, Wasi Shah, Adnan Baig, Shakeel Jazib, Ashfaq Nasir, Saima Aftab, Rehman Faris, Zarnigar Abbas and Saba Uddin Hunzai. Spanning the classical and the contemporary, their readings reflected the range of Urdu poetry and its continuing ability to speak to the present.

“Poetry has always been a meeting place. For five years, Mehfil-e-Sukhan has opened Serena’s doors to the poets who give voice to Pakistan, and to the audiences, from Pakistan and beyond, who come to listen. At its heart, cultural diplomacy is simply that: an invitation to sit together and share in something enduring,” said Mr. Aziz Boolani, Global CEO of Serena Hotels. Since its first edition in 2022, Mehfil-e-Sukhan has become a fixture of the capital’s cultural calendar: a setting in which celebrated poets and appreciative audiences meet in the spirit of the traditional mushaira. Its fifth edition reaffirms Serena’s commitment to keeping Urdu’s literary heritage alive. Mehfil-e-Sukhan forms part of Serena’s wider support for literature and the arts across Pakistan, including the Lahore Literary Festival and the Quetta Literary Festival, which give writers, poets and thinkers a platform to share ideas with wider audiences.

Through its Cultural Diplomacy Initiative, Serena opens its spaces to Pakistan’s artists, writers and thinkers, and to the communities, at home and abroad, who come to meet them. It reflects a belief that understanding between people often begins with shared culture, and that Pakistan’s rich and plural heritage deserves to be celebrated, preserved and heard.

headline: Iran, US continue Doha talks as Tehran warns of wider war
description: TEHRAN - Iran and the United States continued diplomatic efforts to end their eight-month-old conflict on Sunday, as Iranian negotiators held a third
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: TEHRAN - Iran and the United States continued diplomatic efforts to end their eight-month-old conflict on Sunday, as Iranian negotiators held a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha amid growing threats of renewed military confrontation. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said consultations with Qatari officials were ongoing but no final agreement had been reached, stressing that Tehran was prepared for both diplomacy and defence. Speaking to state media, Araghchi said the outcome of the discussions depended on Washington’s response to Iran’s proposals and questions. He maintained that there was no plan to hold direct negotiations with American officials during his latest visit. Iran has insisted on seven conditions for any agreement, with National Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei reiterating that diplomacy would remain an option if Tehran’s demands were met. He warned, however, that any fresh attack on Iran would invite devastating retaliation using new weapons. An official briefed on the discussions told a news wire that Iranian negotiators had been engaged in talks with Qatari mediators for three consecutive days to advance an understanding aimed at ending the US-Israeli war against Iran. Araghchi also indicated that Tehran and Doha had developed a proposal for reopening the strategically important Strait of Hormuz within two days of a potential agreement with Washington. However, diplomatic efforts have been accompanied by increasingly hardline statements from both sides. US President Donald Trump said Washington could strike Iran’s remaining suspected nuclear facilities within minutes, despite describing negotiations as progressing. Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, Trump claimed that American military operations had severely weakened Iran’s armed forces and nuclear infrastructure, leaving only one or two targets requiring further action. He specifically mentioned the suspected underground nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain, saying the United States could deal with the remaining sites quickly. Iran has denied conducting nuclear activities at the facility. Trump said Washington was not in a hurry to reach an agreement but reiterated that Iran would never be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons. He also declined to rule out renewed military action, saying he could not disclose whether strikes might resume in the coming days. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not made a decision about further attacks and preferred a diplomatic settlement. Meanwhile, US Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs Donald Blome warned that Washington was prepared to consider other options if normal navigation through the Strait of Hormuz was not restored. Speaking at the Manama Dialogue security forum in Bahrain, Blome said diplomatic channels remained open but stressed that the United States would not allow Iran to hold the region and global economy hostage. Iran, meanwhile, has stepped up military preparedness. Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi said Tehran was rapidly enhancing its armed forces’ combat capabilities to enable them to respond without geographical limitations. He said the military was strengthening its smart combat capabilities under directives from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, warning that any attack would receive an appropriate and decisive response. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Deputy for Political Affairs Brigadier General Yadollah Javani said Iranian forces were operating on the assumption that the United States or Israel could launch an attack at any moment. He claimed Iran’s military capabilities allowed it to respond through defensive, pre-emptive and offensive operations, warning that any area entered by enemy forces could become a “killing ground”. Iranian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia also warned that any renewed US aggression would trigger an immediate and decisive response on a larger scale than before. He cautioned that a future conflict would not necessarily remain confined to West Asia. In another development, Iran designated Britain’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organisations and its intelligence agency MI6 as a hostile group, according to the Iranian Foreign Ministry. The decision was announced in response to Britain’s designation of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organisation under the State Threats Act 2026 on July 13. Tehran also accused London of supporting the US-Israeli military campaign by providing access to military and logistical facilities under British jurisdiction. Iran has separately submitted documents and photographic evidence of alleged US and Israeli attacks on its ports, civilian vessels and maritime infrastructure to the International Maritime Organisation, warning that damage to navigation and rescue systems could endanger shipping and seafarers across the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Sea of Oman. Regional countries have expressed concern over the possibility of another escalation. UAE presidential diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash said Abu Dhabi hoped negotiations would produce a diplomatic breakthrough but was prepared for the worst. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah television reported that two air raids had targeted an oil facility in the Bajil district of western Hodeidah governorate, wounding at least three civilians. There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition. The diplomatic efforts come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the November 3 US midterm elections. Trump has indicated that Washington would refrain from launching fresh attacks before the vote, while Tehran has warned that any new confrontation could be longer and more extensive than the previous conflict. The continuing tensions have disrupted global oil supplies and raised fears of a wider regional crisis, with the future of the Strait of Hormuz emerging as a central issue in negotiations.

headline: Saudi-led coalition launches operation to ‘neutralise’ Houthi military resources
description: RIYADH - The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday that it had carried out a military operation to “neutralise vital resources” used by the Houthi
author: News Source
article_text: RIYADH - The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday that it had carried out a military operation to “neutralise vital resources” used by the Houthi group to support its war effort and strengthen its military capabilities, particularly ballistic missiles and drones. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that the operation took place on Sunday morning following continued Houthi attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. The coalition’s joint forces command had monitored the Houthis’ “continued use of vital resources to support their war effort and bolster their military capabilities, especially ballistic missiles and drones,” he said. Al-Maliki said the continued attacks posed a direct threat to civilian lives and the safety of civilian infrastructure. The operation sought to “neutralise” resources used by the group to carry out repeated attacks and threaten the security of Saudi Arabia and Yemen, as well as shipping lanes in the southern Red Sea, he added. The statement did not identify the targeted locations or specify the nature of the resources it said had been neutralised. It also provided no details on casualties or material damage. There was no immediate comment from the Houthis. Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation “Dawn of Yemen” to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa. Military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports. The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement. Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government. A strike at an industrial complex in Saudi Arabia’s Dammam caused a huge fire on Sunday, Iran’s state-run IRNA Nerecognisedws Agency reported. “A Yemeni strike hit an industrial complex in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia, sparking a large fire at the facility,” IRNA said in a post on X. A drone belonging to Yemen’s Houthi group struck a family home in the Old Airport neighbourhood in western Taiz city, according to Al Jazeera, reportedly killing a mother and daughter. The development comes amid escalating hostilities between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s internationally recognised government. The two sides have exchanged daily attacks since a fragile truce collapsed over the summer. The Houthis on Thursday reported that 12 people had been killed and three others critically injured in what they described as Saudi strikes on residential areas in western Yemen. The group’s health ministry said the casualties occurred when homes belonging to two families were targeted in Al-Barah, in Maqbana district. The claims could not be independently verified. The Houthis had reported at least 14 deaths in Saudi strikes on a petrol station and market on Wednesday, while the group also targeted the airport in Aden, a stronghold of Yemen’s internationally recognised government, wounding civilians. The latest escalation follows a breakdown of the 2022 truce in July, after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace. The move triggered renewed attacks, with the rebels subsequently targeting Saudi territory, shipping and oil facilities. The Houthis have also intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and prompted the cancellation of major events, threatening the kingdom’s economic diversification plans. Yemen has endured conflict since 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year in support of the government. More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since hostilities resumed, according to United Nations figures. Separately, Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council issued two decrees on Sunday appointing new governors for al-Bayda in central Yemen and al-Jawf in the north, two provinces partially controlled by the Houthis. The government-run version of Saba News Agency said that Major General Hussein al-Ajji Ali al-Awadhi was appointed as governor of al-Bayda. Major General Amin Ali al-Akimi was also named as governor of al-Jawf and commander of its military axis, the agency added. Al-Awadhi replaces former al-Bayda governor Nasser al-Sawadi, while al-Akimi takes over al-Jawf from al-Awadhi, who had served as the province’s governor. The appointments come as both provinces face a complex military situation, with clashes continuing between government forces and the Houthi group over control of strategic positions. The Houthis control most areas of al-Bayda, while control of al-Jawf is divided between the group and government forces. Al-Bayda holds strategic importance because of its central location in Yemen and its borders with eight other provinces, four in the north and four in the south. Al-Jawf is also of military and geographic significance because it shares a land border with Saudi Arabia and lies near the Houthi-controlled provinces of Saada, Amran and Sanaa. It also borders Marib and Hadhramaut, which are under government control. Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation “Dawn of Yemen” to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa. Military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports. The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement. Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

headline: Pakistan Water Week 2026 kicks off today in capital
description: ISLAMABAD - Preparations have been completed for the 6th Pakistan Water Week 2026, which will kick off in Islamabad on November 2 to bring national and
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Preparations have been completed for the 6th Pakistan Water Week 2026, which will kick off in Islamabad on November 2 to bring national and international stakeholders together to advance water security and climate-resilient food systems. The five-day international conference, themed “Commitments to Action: Advancing Water Security and Achieving Climate-Resilient Food Systems in Pakistan,” will continue until November 6. The event is being organised by the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), in collaboration with the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) and the Ministry of Water Resources. The conference will bring together policymakers, parliamentarians, researchers, development partners, youth leaders, civil society representatives and media professionals, with participation available both in person and online.

It will feature two parallel thematic tracks, each comprising 13 sessions, focusing on strengthening water, agriculture and food systems through effective policy implementation and scaling up inclusive innovations for climate resilience. Key topics to be discussed include groundwater management, irrigation reforms, drought and health, climate financing, Pakistan’s preparations for COP31, the water-energy-food-environment nexus, artificial intelligence, digital twins, cryosphere risks in the Upper Indus Basin, and women’s and youth leadership in water security. Three plenary sessions will focus on development partners’ priorities in water and climate, water governance in the Indus Basin, and Australian water innovations for the basin. IWMI Director General Dr. Mark Smith will join the second-day plenary panel online alongside national and international experts. International participants will also visit a water body during a study tour scheduled for the final day of the conference. Dr. Mohsin Hafeez, Strategic Program Director for Water, Food and Ecosystems at IWMI said that Pakistan already has many of the policies, laws and plans it needs. The real challenge is implementation.

He said the conference aimed to bridge the gap between evidence and decision-making by linking policy commitments with practical action on the ground. IWMI Country Representative for Pakistan Dr. Muhammad Ashraf told APP that water security had become central to Pakistan’s food security, economy and climate resilience. He said the conference would bring science, policy and practice together to identify priorities, determine responsibilities and establish mechanisms to track progress. The event is supported by PCRWR through the Ministry of The event is supported by PCRWR through the Ministry of Water Resources, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR), the CGIAR Policy Innovations Science Program, and the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).

headline: CBD Punjab COO reviews site clearance, development plans for proposed Diplomatic Enclave
description: LAHORE - Chief Operating Officer of Punjab Central Business District Development Authority (PCBDDA), also known as Central Business District Punjab (CBD
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - Chief Operating Officer of Punjab Central Business District Development Authority (PCBDDA), also known as Central Business District Punjab (CBD Punjab), Brigadier (R) Mansoor Janjua visited the site of the proposed Diplomatic Enclave in CBD Bab District to review the progress of site clearance and receive a detailed briefing on the project’s design and upcoming development phases. During the visit, Director Project Management Asif Iqbal, Director Marketing Waseem Siddiq, Director Construction Asif Babar, and other senior officials of CBD Punjab were also present.

The COO CBD Punjab was briefed on the progress of site clearance activities and informed that the site clearance work had been completed. He was further apprised that construction activities would commence shortly in accordance with the approved design. The briefing also covered various aspects of the project, including its proposed architectural design, development framework and conceptual layout, which were presented through detailed 3D visualizations and renderings. Speaking on the occasion, COO CBD Punjab Brigadier (R) Mansoor Janjua stated that the Diplomatic Enclave is a significant and forward-looking initiative of CBD Punjab, envisioned to provide Punjab with a distinctive identity on the international stage. headline: Pakistan assumes G-24 chairmanship
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24), reiterating its pledge to strengthening the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24), reiterating its pledge to strengthening the collective voice of developing economies and advancing a fair and development-oriented international financial system, the finance ministry said on Sunday. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb described the chairmanship as a profound responsibility, calling for renewed international cooperation, stronger multilateral institutions and reinforced global commitments to address climate shocks, development financing gaps and global economic fragmentation, according to the finance ministry. The future of developing economies is not peripheral to the future of the global economy. It is central to it,” Aurangzeb said, highlighting the immense potential of emerging and developing nations as drivers of investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and global growth. The finance czar outlined three priorities: development-led growth, stronger representation for developing economies and reform of international financial architecture. Aurangzeb said that Pakistan, as the G-24 chair, will prioritise placing development at the centre of global economic policymaking. He stressed that macroeconomic stability must serve as a foundation for investment, productivity, employment and shared prosperity, enabling developing and low-income economies to move beyond crisis management towards sustainable growth. Secondly, Aurangzeb said that Pakistan would advocate for strengthening multilateral frameworks for the collective benefit of members through more inclusive and representative institutions. Pakistan will advocate for more equitable and fair governance, meaningful participation in decision-making and greater responsiveness of the Bretton Woods institutions to the evolving needs and realities of their members, he added. The country’s third priority as the G-24 chairman will be advancing a development-oriented international financial architecture. Priorities will include affordable and timely development financing, sustainable debt solutions, stronger global financial safety nets, climate resilience and greater mobilisation of public and private capital, he said. “Our task is to ensure that the immense potential of developing economies is not constrained by an international financial architecture that has yet to fully adapt to a changing world,” he emphasised. ‘Necessary financing’ Drawing on Pakistan’s own experience of economic stabilisation, reform and resilience, the finance minister underscored the importance of aligning financial stability with long-term development objectives, while ensuring that reforming economies have the necessary financing and policy space to pursue sustainable growth. He reaffirmed that Pakistan’s chairmanship would be guided by the G-24’s longstanding principles of consultation, consensus and collective advocacy, working closely with members across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, alongside the IMF, World Bank and other international partners, to translate shared priorities into practical outcomes. Senator Aurangzeb also acknowledged Nigeria’s leadership as outgoing chair and expressed Pakistan’s commitment to building on the Group’s progress. The finance minister stressed that the effectiveness of collective leadership must be judged by tangible development outcomes. “The true measure of our collective leadership will not simply be the strength of our voice, but the difference that voice makes,” he stated. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to advancing the G-24’s mission “from collective voice to collective influence, and from collective influence to meaningful progress.” Meanwhile, Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday termed Pakistan’s election as chairman of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) an important diplomatic milestone, stating it would further strengthen the country’s voice and role in global economic affairs. According to a spokesperson, expressing deep pleasure over the achievement, the Prime Minister commended Finance Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and the entire Ministry of Finance team for their tireless efforts, effective diplomacy, and professional capabilities. He appreciated the Finance Minister and his team for their proactive role during the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), noting that their efforts helped secure a prominent position for Pakistan in providing economic leadership to developing nations. The Prime Minister said the G-24 chairmanship would provide Pakistan with an influential platform to advocate for essential reforms in the global financial system, ensure equitable financial assistance to combat climate change, and foster sustainable development opportunities for emerging economies.

headline: From fear to recovery: PM’s Hepatitis C Programme brings hope of life and recovery to millions
description: ISLAMABAD - For millions who risk losing their lives to hepatitis C simply because they cannot afford its diagnosis and treatment, the Prime
author: Yawar Abbas
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - For millions who risk losing their lives to hepatitis C simply because they cannot afford its diagnosis and treatment, the Prime Minister’s Programme for the Elimination of Hepatitis C has emerged as a beacon of hope, offering free screening, medicines and treatment to save lives and protect families from the devastating consequences of the disease.

Hepatitis C has long been a silent threat, often discovered when the disease has already begun damaging the liver. For poor families, the fear of diagnosis is compounded by the inability to afford expensive medical tests and treatment. Now, the Prime Minister’s National Programme for the Elimination of Hepatitis C is offering a new ray of hope, bringing free screening, diagnosis and treatment within the reach of people who might otherwise remain untreated and vulnerable to life-threatening complications.

The programme represents a significant step towards protecting lives and ensuring that poverty does not deprive anyone of the opportunity to recover from a disease that is now largely curable with modern medicines. The scale of the challenge is enormous. Around 60 million people worldwide, including an estimated 11 million in Pakistan, are affected by hepatitis C. Transmitted primarily through infected blood, contaminated syringes and improperly sterilized or shared blades, the disease is often described as a silent killer because it can remain undetected for years before causing serious liver complications, including cirrhosis and liver cancer.

Despite its potentially devastating consequences, hepatitis C is curable in most cases, making early diagnosis and timely treatment essential to saving lives. Recognizing the financial barriers faced by millions of Pakistanis, the government has introduced free screening, diagnostic testing and treatment under the Prime Minister’s initiative. Under the programme, patients are being provided free PCR diagnostic tests, which normally cost around Rs 8,000, while treatment worth approximately Rs 34,000 to Rs 68,000 is also being provided without charge. For low-income families, this financial support represents substantial relief. Many patients postpone medical examinations or avoid treatment altogether because they cannot afford diagnostic tests and medicines. By removing these financial barriers, the programme aims to ensure that economic hardship does not become a reason for preventable illness, liver complications or loss of life.

Initially launched in Islamabad, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the programme is envisaged to extend its free screening and treatment facilities across the country, bringing millions of people within the reach of essential healthcare services. Health Ministry officials say the programme is designed to address the disease through a comprehensive approach involving mass screening, early diagnosis, treatment, public awareness and systematic follow-up of patients. They said hepatitis C often remains undetected for years because infected individuals may not experience noticeable symptoms during the early stages. By the time complications emerge, the disease may have progressed to serious liver damage, cirrhosis or even liver cancer.

An official of the Ministry of National Health Services said the government’s priority was to ensure that financial constraints did not prevent anyone from accessing essential healthcare. “The programme is based on the principle that every citizen deserves access to screening and treatment, irrespective of their financial circumstances. No person should lose their life simply because they cannot afford a diagnostic test or medicines,” the official said. The District Health Office (DHO) Islamabad is also playing an important role in taking the initiative to communities through free screening facilities, awareness activities and coordination with public sector institutions.

DHO officials said screening activities were being conducted at designated healthcare facilities and through special camps to facilitate people who might otherwise not approach hospitals for testing. They said the office had also extended screening services to parliamentarians and staff members of the National Assembly Secretariat under the directions of Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal. According to DHO officials, free screening, treatment and medicines are available under the programme, while public awareness is being strengthened to encourage people to undergo testing without fear or hesitation. “Early diagnosis is the most effective way to prevent the complications associated with hepatitis C. Our objective is to reach people before the disease progresses and ensure that those testing positive are connected with treatment facilities,” a DHO official said.

The programme has established 17 screening points in Islamabad, while the government is working to expand screening coverage across the country. The ministry has also been pursuing a coordinated approach to reach priority populations and ensure that diagnosed patients complete their treatment. Medical experts believe the initiative could substantially reduce the country’s hepatitis C burden if accompanied by sustained screening, public awareness and strict infection-prevention measures. Dr Maqsood Malik, a senior liver specialist, said hepatitis C was a curable disease in most cases, provided patients were diagnosed and completed the recommended course of treatment. “One of the biggest challenges is that people often discover the infection at an advanced stage. Modern antiviral medicines can cure the majority of hepatitis C patients, usually through a relatively short treatment course.”

The most important step is to identify infected individuals early and ensure that they receive proper medical care, the doctor said. Dr Tauqeer Ahad, another physician associated with public healthcare services, highlighted the importance of free screening, particularly for people from low-income backgrounds. “Many patients avoid diagnostic tests because of financial difficulties. When screening and treatment are provided free of cost, it removes a major barrier to healthcare. This programme can save thousands of families from the financial and emotional consequences of a serious illness,” the doctor said. Dr Naila Shamim, a medical expert, emphasized that treatment alone would not be sufficient without preventive measures and public awareness. “Hepatitis C spreads primarily through contact with infected blood, including the use of contaminated syringes, unsafe medical procedures and improperly sterilized instruments. People must avoid sharing needles and razors, ensure the use of sterile medical equipment and seek screening whenever they have a potential exposure,” the doctor said. The expert added that community awareness, safe blood transfusion practices, infection-control standards in healthcare facilities and responsible medical practices were essential to preventing new infections. The programme’s expansion to Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir is particularly significant, as residents of remote mountainous communities often face geographical and financial challenges in accessing specialized healthcare facilities.

By extending screening and treatment services to these regions, the government aims to reduce disparities in healthcare access and ensure that people living outside major urban centres also benefit from the national elimination initiative. Another important aspect is the use of coordinated patient-tracking mechanisms to improve follow-up and ensure that people diagnosed with hepatitis C are not lost between screening and treatment. The ministry is also working towards strengthening coordination among healthcare institutions to improve programme implementation. Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal has emphasized the need for nationwide screening and a coordinated response to eliminate hepatitis C. The government has also highlighted the scale of the challenge, with millions of Pakistanis estimated to be living with the infection. For the programme to achieve its intended objectives, continuity will be crucial. Regular screening, uninterrupted availability of medicines, reliable diagnostic facilities, trained healthcare workers and effective monitoring will determine its long-term success, Dr Saeed Kareem, a social activist, said. He said that for a daily-wage worker unable to afford expensive medical investigations, a mother worried about her family’s health or an elderly person who has postponed testing for years, “free screening and treatment can mean the difference between prolonged suffering and recovery.”

“If implemented effectively and sustained through strong institutional commitment, the Prime Minister’s National Programme for the Elimination of Hepatitis C could become one of Pakistan’s most consequential public health interventions, protecting lives, relieving poor families of medical expenses and bringing the country closer to the goal of a hepatitis C-free Pakistan,” Dr Kareem said.

author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ATLANTA - United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a press briefing on Saturday said Washington had “obviously heard” Pakistan’s concerns regarding terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, adding that “if there’s a productive role for us to play, we’ll play it.” “Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan,” Rubio said, addressing a briefing in Atlanta, Georgia. He added that Islamabad felt “as though the Taliban have not done enough to constrain those attacks and they’ve taken action against it.” The secretary of state added, “We obviously have heard those concerns on their part, we obviously don’t want them to be targeted.” He also noted that Washington didn’t “necessarily have the closest relationship with the Taliban,” but that “we’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to.” Rubio concluded, “We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets.” His remarks came amid strained relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan. Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story. Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support. Security officials estimate that up to 70% of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan. The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan. In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities. Marco Rubio said US President Donald Trump hasn’t made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks. “We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn’t made a decision. I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Rubio said at a G20 press conference in Atlanta. The top US diplomat added that Trump prefers a diplomatic solution but stresses he believes that “if we needed to do something military, we would have the ability to do it… but we would prefer to do it peacefully.” Rubio also says: “What the Iranian regime is basically arguing is, ‘Unless we get what we want, not only will we blow up ships but we will destroy the energy infrastructure of our neighbours and the entire region.’ Just think about that because I think we just skip over that like it’s some normal behaviour.”

PAKISTAN RESPONDS TO UNPROVOKED FIRING FROM AFGHAN POSTS: DC

Pakistani security forces have responded to unprovoked firing from the Afghan border posts, the deputy commissioner of Lower South Waziristan district said on Sunday. In a post on X, the DC’s official account said, “Unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts onto Pakistani border checkpoints continues.” It added that Pakistani security forces responded immediately and effectively, targeting “multiple Afghan border posts, mortar positions, and defensive checkpoints”. “The Afghan Taliban were forced to abandon their posts and flee in response to the Pakistani forces’ strong response,” the post read. It further said no reports of any casualties have emerged from the border areas on the Pakistani side. “Pakistani forces remain prepared to deliver a full response to any kind of aggression,” the deputy commissioner affirmed. The military’s media affairs wing, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), is yet to comment on the development. The fresh exchange of fire follows Friday’s skirmishes, when Pakistan’s armed forces responded to unprovoked firing from the other side, state media reported, citing security sources. As a result, several Afghan Taliban posts in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar were destroyed. The Afghan forces had also opened fire along the Angoor Adda border area on Tuesday, which claimed the life of one local and injured a family of five. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had condemned the firing, asserting that Pakistan would “never tolerate” attacks on its people or violations of its sovereignty. Pakistan had also dismissed a statement by Afghanistan’s defence ministry regarding the incident that claimed that Pakistan was the aggressor, terming it a “fabrication of lies”. Amid the heightened tensions, United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday said that Washington has “heard” Pakistan’s concerns about terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and if “there’s a productive role for us to play, we would play it”. Asked about the conflict between the neighbouring countries, Rubio said, “We’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to. We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets.”

Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.

Security officials estimate that up to 70% of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.

The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.

In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.

Marco Rubio said US President Donald Trump hasn’t made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks.

“We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn’t made a decision. I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Rubio said at a G20 press conference in Atlanta.

The top US diplomat added that Trump prefers a diplomatic solution but stresses he believes that “if we needed to do something military, we would have the ability to do it… but we would prefer to do it peacefully.”

Rubio also says: “What the Iranian regime is basically arguing is, ‘Unless we get what we want, not only will we blow up ships but we will destroy the energy infrastructure of our neighbours and the entire region.’ Just think about that because I think we just skip over that like it’s some normal behaviour.”
PAKISTAN RESPONDS TO UNPROVOKED FIRING FROM AFGHAN POSTS: DC

Pakistani security forces have responded to unprovoked firing from the Afghan border posts, the deputy commissioner of Lower South Waziristan district said on Sunday.

In a post on X, the DC’s official account said, “Unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts onto Pakistani border checkpoints continues.”

It added that Pakistani security forces responded immediately and effectively, targeting “multiple Afghan border posts, mortar positions, and defensive checkpoints”.

“The Afghan Taliban were forced to abandon their posts and flee in response to the Pakistani forces’ strong response,” the post read.

It further said no reports of any casualties have emerged from the border areas on the Pakistani side.

“Pakistani forces remain prepared to deliver a full response to any kind of aggression,” the deputy commissioner affirmed.

The military’s media affairs wing, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), is yet to comment on the development.

The fresh exchange of fire follows Friday’s skirmishes, when Pakistan’s armed forces responded to unprovoked firing from the other side, state media reported, citing security sources. As a result, several Afghan Taliban posts in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar were destroyed.

The Afghan forces had also opened fire along the Angoor Adda border area on Tuesday, which claimed the life of one local and injured a family of five.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had condemned the firing, asserting that Pakistan would “never tolerate” attacks on its people or violations of its sovereignty.

Pakistan had also dismissed a statement by Afghanistan’s defence ministry regarding the incident that claimed that Pakistan was the aggressor, terming it a “fabrication of lies”.

Amid the heightened tensions, United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday said that Washington has “heard” Pakistan’s concerns about terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and if “there’s a productive role for us to play, we would play it”.

Asked about the conflict between the neighbouring countries, Rubio said, “We’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to. We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets.”

headline: KPT handles two bulk carriers carrying 101,000 tonnes of fertiliser, wheat: Junaid Anwar
description: ISLAMABAD - Karachi Port Trust (KPT) has simultaneously handled two foreign bulk carriers carrying a combined 101,000 tonnes of diammonium phosphate (DAP)
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Karachi Port Trust (KPT) has simultaneously handled two foreign bulk carriers carrying a combined 101,000 tonnes of diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertiliser and wheat, Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry said on Sunday.

The minister commended KPT engineers, port operators? pilots, terminal operator, dockworkers and transporters for managing the two vessels and maintaining cargo discharge operations. He said the timely handling of essential imports was important for supporting agricultural production and ensuring food security. The two vessels, MV ZHONG CHANG 538 and MV GOKOVA M, carrying 50,000 tonnes of DAP fertiliser and 51,000 tonnes of wheat, respectively, were berthed at Karachi Gateway Terminal Multipurpose (KG?ML).

According to KPT operational data, MV ZHONG CHANG 538 was berthed at Berth 10/11 with its 50,000-tonne DAP consignment. Of the total cargo, 48,525 tonnes had been discharged, bringing unloading operations close to completion. The vessel recorded a discharge rate of 5,481 tonnes during the preceding 24 hours. Meanwhile, MV GOKOVA M, carrying 51,000 tonnes of wheat, was berthed at Berth 16/17. More than 7,200 tonnes had been discharged, while unloading operations were continuing. Junaid Chaudhry said the simultaneous handling of the two vessels reflected KPT’s operational capacity and efforts to improve berth utilisation, cargo-handling efficiency and supply chain performance.

He said the Ministry of Maritime Affairs was pursuing reforms to reduce vessel turnaround times, improve port management and strengthen maritime infrastructure to facilitate international trade and ensure the uninterrupted supply of essential commodities.

“Efficient port operations and streamlined logistics are essential for ensuring the timely movement of critical commodities and strengthening supply chains,” he said. KPT Chairman Rear Admiral Shahid Ahmed said Karachi Port played a vital role in the country’s trade and supply chain network, particularly in facilitating imports of agricultural inputs and essential food commodities. The vessels were given priority berthing on the government’s dircetives. He said the port authority was committed to modernising infrastructure, improving operational efficiency and expanding cargo-handling capacity to support trade and economic activity.

headline: Wedding stampede leaves 1 dead, 18 injured; 6 arrested
description: SIALKOT - Police arrested six suspects following a severe stampede that left one person dead and 18 others injured during a wedding function at Faraz
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
SIALKOT - Police arrested six suspects following a severe stampede that left one person dead and 18 others injured during a wedding function at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road. According to a spokesperson on Sunday, the victim was identified as Aqeel, son of Bashir Ahmed. All 18 injured individuals were shifted to nearby hospitals by Rescue 1122 and discharged after receiving necessary medical treatment.

According to police, First Information Report (FIR No. 1335/26) was registered at Motra Police Station on the complaint of SHO Inspector Mubeen Ahmed Cheema against nine nominated individuals—including event organizer Ansar Mahmood alias ‘Mr Patlu’, Kashif, ground owner Haji Shahid Javed, and co-organizers Daniyal, Munir Ahmed, Mohsin Ali, Irshad Ali, Abdullah, and Zohaib Mansha—along with 40 to 45 unidentified security guards. The case has been filed under Sections 322, 431, 440, 188, 109, 148, and 149 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) and Section 16 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO). Preliminary police investigations revealed that the organizers had announced a lucky draw on social media featuring cars, motorcycles, and other valuable prizes, attracting an unexpectedly huge crowd. The stampede was triggered when an announcement was made over the loudspeaker directing participants to enter the ground simultaneously.

Police stated that organizers committed severe violations of SOPs and event permission conditions, resulting in civil disturbance, damage to public property, and massive traffic blockades along main Daska-Sialkot Road. DPO Sialkot Captain (retd) Dost Muhammad personally supervised the emergency rescue operations, cleared ambulance access routes, and oversaw crowd control alongside heavy police contingents and Elite Force personnel. Reiterating a strict stance, DPO Dost Muhammad stated that negligence regarding safety protocols at public gatherings would not be tolerated and vowed that all accused individuals would face unbiased legal action strictly on merit. Raids are currently underway to arrest the remaining fleeing suspects.

headline: PPP urges opposition to end boycott, join electoral reforms process
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) yesterday called for comprehensive electoral reforms and urged the opposition to resume its role in
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) yesterday called for comprehensive electoral reforms and urged the opposition to resume its role in parliamentary committees. The PPP stressed that democratic traditions, constitutional supremacy and responsible parliamentary engagement were essential for a strong and stable state.

PPP Parliamentarians Secretary General Syed Nayyer Hussain Bukhari said the PPP believed in a strong state, the supremacy of the Constitution and the promotion of democratic parliamentary traditions. He said the party’s political vision was centred on building a strong and stable Pakistan, adding that the PPP had the distinction of giving the country its Constitution. In a statement, he said PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari wanted opposition parties to be represented in the parliamentary committee on electoral reforms to ensure an inclusive process and strengthen confidence in the country’s electoral system.

Recalling the parliamentary role of former prime minister Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto, Bukhari said she had effectively performed the role of opposition despite having only 17 seats in parliament, demonstrating the importance of constructive parliamentary engagement regardless of numerical strength. He described parliamentary committees as an integral part of legislation and democratic governance, arguing that meaningful participation by all parliamentary parties was necessary for effective lawmaking. However, he maintained that the demand for equal representation in committees, irrespective of the parties’ representation in parliament, was not consistent with the principle of proportional representation. Bukhari said the PPP wanted opposition parties to return to parliamentary committees and fulfil their constitutional and democratic responsibilities rather than remain disengaged from the legislative process.

Expressing concern over the delay in electoral reforms, he pointed out that despite the passage of two and a half years, legislation to reform electoral laws had yet to be undertaken. He stressed the need for effective implementation of electoral reforms, along with appropriate legal provisions to ensure accountability through a fair system of rewards and penalties. He said comprehensive electoral reforms would help minimise controversies, allegations and disputes following elections, while the opposition’s participation would make the legislative process more inclusive and credible.

Urging political parties to move beyond confrontation, Bukhari said the attitude of refusing to accept every initiative should be abandoned in favour of a responsible and constructive role in parliament. He also called on the Leader of the Opposition to engage with the prime minister over the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and two members of the Election Commission of Pakistan, emphasising that the constitutional process required consultation between the two offices.

“The Prime Minister House and the chambers of the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition are not anyone’s personal property; these are offices of the state,” he said, underscoring the institutional nature of parliamentary responsibilities.

Bukhari cautioned against the use of indecorous language in political discourse, saying such conduct undermined parliamentary traditions and weakened the democratic culture that political parties should collectively uphold.

headline: Islamabad Police facilitation vans to serve citizens at 18 locations from today
description: ISLAMABAD - Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Police have issued a six-day schedule for their mobile facilitation vans, which will provide driving
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Police have issued a six-day schedule for their mobile facilitation vans, which will provide driving licence and other police services to citizens at 18 locations across the federal capital from November 2 to 7.

An ICT Police official told that, three mobile units, including a Police Station on Wheels and two facilitation vans, will visit different educational institutions, residential areas and public places to provide services at citizens’ doorsteps.

He said the mobile units would operate daily from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, offering services such as missing reports, police character certificates, learner driving permits, licence renewals and duplicate driving licences.

The official said the two facilitation vans would also provide driving test sheets and other licence-related services.

On Monday, November 2, the Police Station on Wheels will be stationed at Iqra University, H-9; Van-I at Federal Urdu University, Islamabad; and Van-II at FAST University, H-11.

On Tuesday, November 3, the units will be available at COMSATS University, Park Road; National University of Technology (NUTECH), I-12; and National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), H-12, respectively.

On Wednesday, November 4, the mobile units will visit Government Degree College for Boys, Thanda Pani; International Islamic University, H-10; and Capital University of Science and Technology (CUST), Islamabad Expressway.

On Thursday, November 5, the units will be stationed at National University of Modern Languages (NUML), H-9/4; International Islamic University, H-10; and PWD Market near Patiala Jewellers.

On Friday, November 6, the mobile units will provide services at Riphah University, I-14; Air Headquarters, E-9; and Rangers Headquarters, Bari Imam.

On Saturday, November 7, the units will visit Kirpa Village; Benazir Chowk, Tarnol; and DHA Phase 5, Gate 1. The official said citizens could contact the facilitation service in-charge, Sub-Inspector Nazia Rafique, at 0313-6260626 for further information.

He said the Police Station on Wheels could be contacted at 0313-5235946, Van-I at 0315-5798711 and Van-II at 0300-2322883.

headline: Pharmacists warned against obtaining multiple drug sale licences
description: ISLAMABAD - The Pharmacy Services and Drug Control Wing of the Health Department, Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) has warned pharmacists against
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Pharmacy Services and Drug Control Wing of the Health Department, Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) has warned pharmacists against obtaining or holding multiple drug sale licences against a single professional registration, declaring the practice illegal and professionally unacceptable.

According to official sources, in a public and professional advisory, the department stated that each pharmacist must hold and utilize only one drug sale licence.

It advised all applicants to ensure full disclosure, provide accurate information and strictly comply with applicable laws and regulations while applying for licences. The department warned that any violation would invite appropriate legal and regulatory action.

It also urged pharmacy professionals to uphold ethical standards, protect the dignity of the profession and ensure compliance with relevant regulations.

headline: Attock journalists announce peaceful protest during CM Punjab’s visit
description: ATTOCK - The journalist community of Attock has announced to hold a peaceful protest on the occasion of the visit of Chief Minister Punjab
author: Muhammad Sabrin
article_text: ATTOCK - The journalist community of Attock has announced to hold a peaceful protest on the occasion of the visit of Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif to highlight their long-standing demand for a Press Club building. The journalists said they have been deprived of a Press Club building for more than a decade despite repeated assurances by the district administration. Senior journalists Syed Raza Naqvi, Sheikh Javed Iqbal, Sheikh Faisal Javed, Hafiz Shahzad Akhtar, Muhammad Sabrin, Karim Khan, Dr. Waheed Khattak and others said that no practical step has been taken for the provision of Press Club building. They said that the peaceful protest in front of a public representative is not a crime and is a democratic right. “We will protest peacefully to highlight our issue and will demand a building for our Press Club as it is our right,” they said.

Senior journalists Syed Raza Naqvi, Sheikh Javed Iqbal, Sheikh Faisal Javed, Hafiz Shahzad Akhtar, Muhammad Sabrin, Karim Khan, Dr. Waheed Khattak and others said that no practical step has been taken for the provision of Press Club building. They said that the peaceful protest in front of a public representative is not a crime and is a democratic right. “We will protest peacefully to highlight our issue and will demand a building for our Press Club as it is our right,” they said.

headline: Aerial firing becomes nuisance for residents

author: APP
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - Aerial firing during celebrations has become a nuisance for residents of the Waris Khan and other areas, creating fear and panic among the public. Residents have expressed concern over the repeated incidents of aerial firing, saying that despite the seriousness of the matter, police have failed to take effective action against those involved. According to residents, aerial firing continues in the area, putting the lives of innocent people at risk. They said the practice not only disturbs the peace but also poses a serious threat to public safety. The residents have urged the police authorities to take notice of the situation, launch action against those involved and ensure an end to the illegal practice.

They have also questioned the lack of police action despite repeated incidents.

headline: Non-academic burden weighs heavy on private school teachers
description: ISLAMABAD - The teachers of leading private schools in the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad are under severe stress as their workload of
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The teachers of leading private schools in the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad are under severe stress as their workload of non-academic and extracurricular activities has increased manifold, relegating their primary task of teaching to the background.

From daily themed activities like Colour Day, Mango Day, Welcome Parties, to week-long preparations for annual functions, sports galas and social media content creation, teachers say they are forced to work beyond their job descriptions without any extra compensation.

Many teachers believe these activities are now being used as a marketing strategy to attract admissions, while the entire burden is placed on the teaching staff.

A female teacher Noshaba at a prominent private school said, “we were appointed to teach, but most of our time is now consumed by classroom decoration, event management, dance rehearsals and making videos for school pages”.

She stated that they have to stay after school hours for preparations. If parents complain about a single picture, the management holds them responsible.

She remarked that earlier, competition among schools was based on academic results. Now it is based on who organizes more colourful functions. In this race, real education is suffering Another teacher Tehreem from a private school in F-8 sector said, “Our official timing is till 1:30 p.m., but during event season we stay till 4 p.m. There is no overtime. Those who refuse to stay face consequences in their evaluation.”

Teachers performing duties as hosts, photographers and crowd managers during Parent-Teacher Meetings and Fun Fairs also complained of exhaustion,she complained.

“On PTM and Fun Gala days, we have to stand for seven to eight hours to manage the rush. The very next day, we are expected to deliver lectures with the same energy in class.

It is extremely tiring,” a teacher from I-8 shared.

headline: Free dead body transportation service inaugurated at Jhelum hospital
description: Jhelum - Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani on Sunday inaugurated a free dead body transportation service at the
author: FASEEH UL HASSAN
article_text:
Jhelum - Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani on Sunday inaugurated a free dead body transportation service at the District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital Jhelum, providing relief to bereaved families by ensuring the transportation of deceased patients to their homes and villages without any charges.

Under the initiative, families of patients who die at the hospital will be provided free ambulance services to transport the bodies to their respective homes, eliminating the financial burden and difficulties associated with arranging private ambulances.

Speaking to the media at the inauguration ceremony, Mr Kayani said the service would spare grieving families the inconvenience of searching for private ambulances and negotiating transportation fares during an already distressing time.

He described the initiative as a commendable step by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif to minimise public difficulties and provide relief to citizens in moments of grief.

The minister said two fully operational ambulances, equipped with the necessary facilities, had initially been allocated for Jhelum. The vehicles had undergone the required modifications, while dedicated staff had also been deployed to ensure the smooth operation of the service. He clarified that the ambulances assigned to the dead body transportation service were additional vehicles and would not affect the routine emergency services of Rescue 1122.

Mr Kayani said separate vehicles and personnel had been allocated for the initiative to ensure that the facility remained available to bereaved families without disrupting other emergency response operations.

headline: Teaching in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
description: Artificial intelligence did not wait for education systems to prepare for it. It simply walked into the classroom. googletag.cmd.push(function() {
author: Muhammad Ali Baig
article_text:
Artificial intelligence did not wait for education systems to prepare for it. It simply walked into the classroom.

Students can now summon explanations, essays, presentations and solutions in seconds. Teachers are therefore confronting a question far more important than whether AI should be allowed in education: how do we teach when information is instant, answers are abundant, and producing a response no longer necessarily proves learning?

Banning AI offers little comfort. Embracing it indiscriminately offers even less. The sensible path lies somewhere between the two, that is to use technology to strengthen learning without allowing it to replace thought.

Pakistan has already begun navigating this transition. In higher education, HEC has introduced a framework for the responsible use of generative AI, while curriculum reforms are increasing creating space for AI-related learning and its educational applications, especially in the context of industrial revolution 5.0. The response has also moved from policy to faculty development. Through its National Academy of Higher Education, HEC has recently trained around 400 lecturers and assistant professors from public-sector universities under its programme, AI Literacy for Educators: Building AI-Ready Institutions. The training combines conceptual understanding with hands-on learning and prepares faculty to critically evaluate and responsibly integrate AI into teaching, learning, research and assessment. It also addresses academic integrity, privacy, intellectual property and discipline-specific applications of AI. AI-supported teacher development is also emerging within the federal education system, while Punjab has announced teacher training alongside its broader move towards AI integration in schools. UNESCO, too, is supporting teacher capacity in Pakistan for ethical and effective use of AI in learning and assessment. These are encouraging beginnings. But technology is moving too quickly for every classroom response to await a policy notification, new funding or a centrally designed program. Much of the adaptation required can and should begin within educational institutions themselves.

For schools, the starting point need not be expensive technology. It can simply be better-prepared teachers. School administrations can organise short learning sessions where teachers explore AI together, demonstrate useful applications and discuss what has worked in their classrooms. A science teacher may use AI to develop differentiated explanations; a language teacher to generate practice exercises; another to demonstrate how confidently AI can sometimes produce an incorrect answer. Schools can develop simple internal norms on responsible use, disclosure, privacy and academic integrity.

The ambition should not be to turn every teacher into an AI specialist. It should be to ensure that every teacher knows enough about AI to exercise professional judgement over its use.

Universities need to go further. They may provide clarity on acceptable AI use while giving disciplines room to determine what makes pedagogical sense. Faculty development should progress from occasional awareness sessions to continuous, practice-oriented learning. Teachers who redesign courses, experiment responsibly with AI, mentor colleagues or demonstrate better learning outcomes may find such efforts recognised in institutional reward systems.

Assessment, however, demands the most urgent rethink.

If a conventional assignment can be completed convincingly by entering its question into an AI tool, the problem may not be the tool only, but the assignment too. More case analysis, projects, presentations, problem-solving, reflection and oral explanation can shift assessment away from reproducing information towards demonstrating understanding.

This is where AI presents an opportunity hidden inside the disruption. For years, educators have argued for moving students from memorisation towards analysis, application and creativity. AI may finally make that transition difficult to postpone.

Why should institutions take the trouble? Because students already inhabit an AI-enabled world, and their future workplaces increasingly will too. The widening gap between how knowledge is produced and used outside educational institutions and how learning is organised inside them cannot be ignored indefinitely. Graduates will need not only to operate AI tools, but to question their outputs, recognise their limitations, exercise judgement and know when human reasoning must take precedence.

Artificial intelligence can produce information. It can generate answers. It can even imitate explanation. But education has always aspired to something deeper: cultivating judgement, curiosity, capability and character. The enduring task of the teacher, therefore, is not threatened by the machine; it is being redefined by it. As AI becomes increasingly capable of providing answers, good teaching must become increasingly capable of producing people who know which questions to ask, which answers to trust, and when to think for themselves.

Muhammad Ali Baig

–The writer is serving as Deputy Director in Higher Education Commission.

author: The Nation
article_text: Isaac Newton’s “Principia Mathematica,” published in 1687, revolutionised our understanding of the physical universe. It laid the groundwork for classical mechanics and introduced Newton’s three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation. Its significance reverberates through history, as it established a framework for scientific inquiry and mathematical rigor that continues to underpin modern physics and engineering. From space exploration to everyday technologies like smartphones and GPS, Newton’s principles are foundational, shaping our understanding of the cosmos and enabling technological advancements that have transformed society. The Principia will always remain a cornerstone of scientific thought, and a crucial part of our journey in understanding the universe.

headline: Ikigai: The Art of Living Longer
description: What can Japan teach Pakistan about finding purpose in life? googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-1681982472501-0'); });
author: The Nation
article_text:
What can Japan teach Pakistan about finding purpose in life?

In a society where success is measured by salary, property, and social status, we rarely ask a more important question: What gives us a reason to wake up every morning? Perhaps the Japanese philosophy of Ikigai offers a different perspective on happiness, purpose and longevity.

In their book Ikigai: The Japanese Secret to a Long and Happy Life, Héctor García and Francesc Miralles explore the lifestyle of Okinawa, particularly the village of Ogimi, known for the longevity of its residents. Their central message is simple: a meaningful life is not necessarily a wealthy one, but one filled with purpose, curiosity and gratitude.

Ikigai refers to a reason for being — something that makes life meaningful. It need not be a grand ambition. It could be raising children, teaching, gardening, writing, or helping others. Purpose is often found in ordinary activities rather than extraordinary achievements.

This idea is particularly relevant to Pakistan, where success is often measured through professional titles, examination results and material possessions. Young people are encouraged to compete and succeed, but rarely taught to find contentment in their work and relationships. Is success meaningful if it leaves us constantly anxious and dissatisfied?

Consider a teacher who encourages a struggling student and helps them realise their potential. The financial rewards may be limited, but knowing that one lesson has influenced a student’s future can provide a deep sense of purpose. This, too, is Ikigai. The philosophy also challenges conventional ideas about retirement. Growing older need not mean giving up productive activities. Reading, mentoring, gardening, and participating in community life can help people maintain a sense of purpose and remain mentally active.

Although Ikigai is not a medical formula for longevity, the book highlights habits associated with healthier living, including regular physical activity, moderate eating, strong friendships and stress management.

For Pakistanis, adopting these habits does not require expensive gym memberships or wellness retreats. Daily walks, home-cooked meals, time with family, and meaningful social connections are practical starting points. We can also replace some of the time spent on social media with activities that bring genuine satisfaction.

Community is another important part of this philosophy. Supportive relationships provide strength during difficult times, and Pakistan’s traditions of visiting relatives and helping neighbours offer opportunities to nurture these bonds. However, busy schedules and digital distractions often weaken social connections.

Ikigai also reminds us not to postpone happiness until we achieve a particular milestone. A promotion, better job or financial security should not determine when we begin enjoying life. Meaning can be found in simple moments, from a morning walk to a meaningful conversation.

Ultimately, Ikigai encourages us to look beyond how long we live and consider how meaningfully we spend our time. We may not control every circumstance, but we can build healthier habits, strengthen relationships, and find activities that give our lives purpose.

Perhaps Pakistan needs to ask a different question: Why do so many of us postpone living until we believe we have succeeded? What is your Ikigai — the reason that makes you welcome another morning?

MUHAMMAD AHMAD MUZAKKI,

Wah Cantt.
