headline: Ahsan Iqbal proposes five political corridors between CPC and Pakistani parties
description: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal has proposed creating five political corridors between the Communist
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal has proposed creating five political corridors between the Communist Party of China (CPC) and Pakistani political parties to expand institutional cooperation and ensure continuity in national development policies.

Speaking at the Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Iqbal said the proposed initiative would include exchanges involving young people and political leaders.

He said Pakistan could draw important lessons from China’s development model, particularly its emphasis on public service, organisational discipline, self-reform, effective governance and long-term planning.

The minister noted that Pakistan had suffered setbacks whenever established development policies were discontinued following changes in government. He stressed that national plans should extend beyond electoral cycles to maintain progress over the long term.

He added that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) was committed to promoting these principles within the country’s democratic system.

Referring to the launch of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) during former prime minister Muhammad Nawaz Sharif’s tenure, Iqbal said its first phase had converted a memorandum of understanding into around $25 billion in investment. He said the projects had added more than 8,000 megawatts of electricity to the national grid, built 888 kilometres of highways and motorways, and created approximately 236,000 direct and indirect jobs.

Reaffirming the longstanding relationship between the two countries, Iqbal said Pakistan-China friendship remained above political differences and changes in government, enjoying broad support among their people.

Discussing URAAN Pakistan and CPEC 2.0, he said the five proposed political corridors would complement the five economic corridors. They would focus on strategic dialogue, governance and development learning, youth and leadership development, cultural links, and regional peace and cooperation.

The minister placed particular emphasis on engaging young people, proposing reciprocal exchanges between emerging leaders from the CPC and Pakistani political parties. The programme could begin with an initial group in 2027, offering participants structured learning opportunities at China’s Central Party School.

Congratulating Chinese President Xi Jinping and the CPC on the conclusion of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee, Iqbal said the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China offered an opportunity to deepen political and institutional ties.

He said leadership should be judged not only by what is achieved during a term in office, but also by the lasting institutions, policies and foundations established for coming generations.

headline: Quaid-e-Azam Trophy to begin on November 3 with 20 regional teams
description: Pakistan’s 69th Quaid-e-Azam Trophy will get underway on November 3, with 20 regional sides set to compete in the Gold and Silver divisions of the country’s
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan’s 69th Quaid-e-Azam Trophy will get underway on November 3, with 20 regional sides set to compete in the Gold and Silver divisions of the country’s premier first-class cricket tournament.

The competition will comprise eight teams in the Gold category and 12 in the Silver event, with a total of 60 matches scheduled across both divisions.

Test captain Babar Azam will feature for Lahore Whites, while ODI skipper Shaheen Shah Afridi will lead FATA in the Gold tournament. The two sides will meet in the opening fixture at Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad on November 3.

Defending champions Karachi Blues will compete in the Gold division alongside Faisalabad, FATA, Lahore Whites, Islamabad, Peshawar, Multan and Sialkot Blues.

The Silver competition has been split into two groups. Lahore Blues, Rawalpindi, Larkana, Quetta, Bahawalpur and Peshawar Whites are placed in Group A, while Group B features Karachi Whites, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Hyderabad, Dera Murad Jamali, Abbottabad and Sialkot Whites.

The Gold tournament will run until December 19, with four matches scheduled in each round. Its final is set to be played from December 15 to 19, with fixtures taking place in Islamabad, Abbottabad and Rawalpindi.

The Silver event will conclude on December 7. Group A matches will be held at the State Bank Ground, UBL Sports Complex and KCCA Stadium in Karachi. Group B fixtures are scheduled for Multan Cricket Stadium, Sports Complex Rahim Yar Khan and Dring Stadium in Bahawalpur.

Gold matches will be staged at National Ground and Diamond Ground in Islamabad, Abbottabad Cricket Stadium and Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi.

The top two teams from the Silver competition will earn promotion to the Gold division for the following season.

headline: PM Shehbaz prioritises SME, housing and agriculture financing to boost jobs and growth
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has said the government’s priority is to strengthen the economy and create employment opportunities for young people by
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has said the government’s priority is to strengthen the economy and create employment opportunities for young people by supporting small and medium enterprises (SMEs), housing and agriculture.

He made the remarks while chairing a meeting to review measures aimed at improving access to credit for these priority sectors.

The prime minister appreciated banks that were effectively extending loans to farmers, businesses and homebuyers under government-backed initiatives.

“Banks that are performing well in facilitating credit provision to agriculture, housing and small and medium enterprises under government initiatives are commendable,” he said.

He directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Ministry of Finance not to extend concessions to banks that were slow in providing loans to farmers, SMEs and consumers under the government’s Apna Ghar scheme.

“The State Bank and the Ministry of Finance should not give concessions to banks that are slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises and consumers under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar scheme, a part of government initiatives,” he added.

Highlighting the role of banks in supporting private-sector growth, Shehbaz urged financial institutions to cooperate in extending credit to priority sectors, just as the government and its departments work with banks.

“Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector. Banks should extend cooperation in providing loans to priority sectors in the same way as the government and its agencies cooperate with banks,” he said.

The prime minister said SMEs could contribute significantly to economic growth, export promotion and job creation. He also described agriculture as the backbone of the national economy, adding that efforts were underway to increase exports through value addition to agricultural products.

“Small and medium enterprises have great potential to grow the economy, promote exports and create employment opportunities. The agriculture sector is the backbone of the country’s economy and efforts are being made to increase exports through value addition of agricultural commodities,” he remarked.

He further said the Apna Ghar scheme would support several industries associated with housing and construction.

“Apna Ghar scheme will promote many industries related to the housing and construction sector,” he said.

Shehbaz directed the finance minister to address financing-related challenges faced by stakeholders in the SME, agriculture and housing sectors and prepare a comprehensive action plan.

He also instructed the SBP and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to work together to resolve tax-related issues affecting SMEs and exporters. The relevant authorities were further asked to develop a risk-coverage strategy to make credit more accessible to small and medium-sized businesses.

During the briefing, officials said the central bank was working on three key areas to expand lending to priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and increasing the use of digital services.

They said the recently launched SME Connect portal, available at smeconnect.sbp.org.pk, would allow business owners to submit loan applications online and track their progress.

The meeting was also informed that the SBP had made progress in expanding financing for housing, agriculture and SMEs.

As of October 23, 2026, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar Programme, with 86,899 applications approved. Of this amount, Rs91 billion had been disbursed to 15,584 applicants.

The total volume of housing finance stood at Rs455 billion, while the number of borrowers benefiting from such loans reached 187,317.

In the agriculture sector, outstanding loans amounted to Rs1,329 billion, benefiting around 3.5 million people. Meanwhile, SME financing reached Rs1,148 billion, with 342,458 entrepreneurs receiving loans.

The government has set a target of increasing lending to both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of the 2026-27 financial year.

Officials also briefed the meeting on risk-sharing and credit-guarantee measures introduced for the housing, agriculture and SME sectors. Work was underway to simplify loan procedures, reduce documentation requirements and improve access to financing through digital platforms.

The participants also reviewed the performance of commercial banks in the three priority sectors, with the prime minister appreciating institutions that had demonstrated stronger results.

Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar and Shaza Fatima Khawaja attended the meeting. Other participants included Prime Minister’s Adviser Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, MNAs Hafeezuddin and Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir, senior officials, and heads and representatives of leading commercial banks.

article_html:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has said the government’s priority is to strengthen the economy and create employment opportunities for young people by supporting small and medium enterprises (SMEs), housing and agriculture.

He made the remarks while chairing a meeting to review measures aimed at improving access to credit for these priority sectors.

The prime minister appreciated banks that were effectively extending loans to farmers, businesses and homebuyers under government-backed initiatives.

“Banks that are performing well in facilitating credit provision to agriculture, housing and small and medium enterprises under government initiatives are commendable,” he said.

Al-Shifa Trust to organize free eye surgical camp

He directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Ministry of Finance not to extend concessions to banks that were slow in providing loans to farmers, SMEs and consumers under the government’s Apna Ghar scheme.

“The State Bank and the Ministry of Finance should not give concessions to banks that are slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises and consumers under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar scheme, a part of government initiatives,” he added.

Highlighting the role of banks in supporting private-sector growth, Shehbaz urged financial institutions to cooperate in extending credit to priority sectors, just as the government and its departments work with banks.

Direct flights imperative to give quantum jump to Pak-Spanish bilateral trade: Carlos Aragon

“Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector. Banks should extend cooperation in providing loans to priority sectors in the same way as the government and its agencies cooperate with banks,” he said.

The prime minister said SMEs could contribute significantly to economic growth, export promotion and job creation. He also described agriculture as the backbone of the national economy, adding that efforts were underway to increase exports through value addition to agricultural products.

“Small and medium enterprises have great potential to grow the economy, promote exports and create employment opportunities. The agriculture sector is the backbone of the country’s economy and efforts are being made to increase exports through value addition of agricultural commodities,” he remarked.

ECP says 1,847 nomination papers issued for Islamabad LG polls over weekend

He further said the Apna Ghar scheme would support several industries associated with housing and construction.

“Apna Ghar scheme will promote many industries related to the housing and construction sector,” he said.

Shehbaz directed the finance minister to address financing-related challenges faced by stakeholders in the SME, agriculture and housing sectors and prepare a comprehensive action plan.

He also instructed the SBP and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to work together to resolve tax-related issues affecting SMEs and exporters. The relevant authorities were further asked to develop a risk-coverage strategy to make credit more accessible to small and medium-sized businesses.

Salman Safdar meets Imran Khan after seven months; PTI forms committee on jail access

During the briefing, officials said the central bank was working on three key areas to expand lending to priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and increasing the use of digital services.

They said the recently launched SME Connect portal, available at smeconnect.sbp.org.pk, would allow business owners to submit loan applications online and track their progress.

The meeting was also informed that the SBP had made progress in expanding financing for housing, agriculture and SMEs.

As of October 23, 2026, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar Programme, with 86,899 applications approved. Of this amount, Rs91 billion had been disbursed to 15,584 applicants.

Petrol price cut by Rs3.40 per litre, diesel by Rs7.76

The total volume of housing finance stood at Rs455 billion, while the number of borrowers benefiting from such loans reached 187,317.

In the agriculture sector, outstanding loans amounted to Rs1,329 billion, benefiting around 3.5 million people. Meanwhile, SME financing reached Rs1,148 billion, with 342,458 entrepreneurs receiving loans.

The government has set a target of increasing lending to both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of the 2026-27 financial year.

Officials also briefed the meeting on risk-sharing and credit-guarantee measures introduced for the housing, agriculture and SME sectors. Work was underway to simplify loan procedures, reduce documentation requirements and improve access to financing through digital platforms.

The participants also reviewed the performance of commercial banks in the three priority sectors, with the prime minister appreciating institutions that had demonstrated stronger results.

Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar and Shaza Fatima Khawaja attended the meeting. Other participants included Prime Minister’s Adviser Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, MNAs Hafeezuddin and Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir, senior officials, and heads and representatives of leading commercial banks.

headline: Melbourne Cup 2026: Flemington prepares for racing’s biggest spectacle
description: Flemington Racecourse is set to take centre stage on Tuesday as the 166th running of the Melbourne Cup brings together 24 of the world’s leading stayers for
author: Muhammad Yashal Mazhar
article_text:
Flemington Racecourse is set to take centre stage on Tuesday as the 166th running of the Melbourne Cup brings together 24 of the world’s leading stayers for Australia’s most prestigious horse-racing event, with a record $10.2 million prize pool at stake.

The Group 1 Lexus Melbourne Cup, contested over 3,200 metres, will headline the Melbourne Cup Carnival, attracting leading international and Australian contenders in a race that traditionally captures the attention of the nation.

This year’s contest promises a compelling international challenge, with Irish trainer Joseph O’Brien bringing a formidable contingent of five runners as he seeks a third Melbourne Cup victory. O’Brien, who previously tasted success with Rekindling in 2017 and Twilight Payment in 2020, will be represented by Trustyourinstinct, Sons And Lovers, Goodie Two Shoes, James J Braddock and Kizlyar.

However, local hopes will be led by trainer Ciaron Maher, who has secured seven places in the final field, underlining his strong presence in Australia’s staying ranks.

Point Of Law has emerged as one of the leading contenders following an impressive Geelong Cup victory. Trained by Maher, the five-year-old will start from barrier nine under jockey Ethan Brown, giving the favourite a potentially favourable position in the 24-horse field.

Trustyourinstinct, ridden by James McDonald, and Hopewell Rock, partnered by Zac Lloyd, are also expected to attract considerable attention, while last year’s runner-up Goodie Two Shoes will be looking to go one better after drawing barrier 19.

The international challenge will face strong competition from established Australian performers, including 2024 Melbourne Cup winner Knight’s Choice, who returns with jockey Robbie Dolan. The pair will start from barrier two as they look to recreate their previous success.

Another notable contender is Middle Earth, who drew the inside barrier for Maher, while James J Braddock faces a difficult assignment after drawing the outside gate at barrier 24.

The $10.2 million prize purse includes $4.5 million for the winner, making the contest one of the richest staying races in international horse racing.

Beyond the sporting spectacle, Melbourne Cup Day remains one of Australia’s biggest annual events, bringing together racing enthusiasts, international visitors and spectators for a celebration that extends well beyond Flemington.

With established champions, emerging contenders and a strong international presence, Tuesday’s race is shaping up as a fascinating contest over the gruelling two-mile distance.

The Melbourne Cup is scheduled to jump at 3 pm AEDT on Tuesday, November 3, as Flemington prepares for another chapter in the history of the race that stops a nation.

headline: IHC directs authorities to complete regularisation process for FIA, NCCIA employees
description: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has directed the authorities to finalise the process for regularising employees of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and
author: APP
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has directed the authorities to finalise the process for regularising employees of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), and submit a detailed report on the interviews conducted and their outcomes.

Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir issued the written order while hearing petitions filed by Tauqeer Jadoon and others, who have sought regularisation of their services.

According to the order, the Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC) submitted its para-wise comments and a report before the court.

headline: Mohammad Amir registers for Afghanistan Premier League as British citizen
description: Former Pakistan fast bowler Mohammad Amir has entered the Afghanistan Premier League (APL) player draft using his British citizenship, following the
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Former Pakistan fast bowler Mohammad Amir has entered the Afghanistan Premier League (APL) player draft using his British citizenship, following the acquisition of a British passport.

According to sources, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has decided against granting no-objection certificates (NOCs) to Pakistani cricketers seeking to participate in the APL.

Several Pakistani players have reportedly registered for the league's draft, which is scheduled to take place tomorrow.

However, Amir's British citizenship means he does not need an NOC from the PCB to take part in the tournament.

headline: German ambassador calls for boosting Pakistan-Germany trade, praises Pakistan’s peace efforts
description: Ambassador of Germany to Pakistan, Dr. Ina Lepel, on Monday emphasized the need to further strengthen economic and trade relations between Pakistan and Germany.
author: APP
article_text: Ambassador of Germany to Pakistan, Dr. Ina Lepel, on Monday emphasized the need to further strengthen economic and trade relations between Pakistan and Germany. She was addressing an interactive session at the National Press Club (NPC), Islamabad, under the club’s international outreach initiative “Meet the Press”. Addressing the gathering, Ambassador Lepel highlighted the longstanding relations between Pakistan and Germany and stressed the need to significantly enhance bilateral trade. She noted that despite the passage of several years, trade figures between the two countries had not witnessed the desired growth. “I served in Pakistan in 2017 and have now returned as ambassador, but unfortunately there has not been significant improvement in bilateral trade volume,” she said. The ambassador stressed that both countries possess immense economic potential and should work closely to expand trade, investment and commercial cooperation for mutual benefit. Speaking on regional issues, Ambassador Lepel appreciated Pakistan’s efforts aimed at reducing tensions in the region, particularly regarding the recent US-Iran standoff. She commended Pakistan’s diplomatic initiatives and efforts to promote peace and dialogue. “I salute Pakistan’s efforts to help achieve peaceful solutions and prevent instability in the region,” she remarked, adding that diplomacy remains the best path to resolving conflicts and avoiding further tensions. The ambassador also spoke about educational opportunities in Germany for Pakistani students. She said Germany remains one of the most preferred destinations for higher education due to its quality institutions, research opportunities, and welcoming academic environment. She informed participants that Germany has increased the number of visas being issued to Pakistani students. However, because of the growing number of applications, processing delays occasionally occur. “There is a huge demand from Pakistani students seeking education in Germany. Sometimes applications take longer because of the volume, but we are working to simplify procedures and make the process more efficient,” she explained. During the interactive session, journalists asked questions on bilateral relations, education, regional security and international developments. Ambassador Lepel responded in detail and emphasized the importance of media, people-to-people contacts and academic exchanges in strengthening ties between Pakistan and Germany. At the conclusion of the visit, NPC President Abdur Razzaq Sial thanked the German ambassador for engaging with the media community and expressed hope that Pakistan-Germany relations would continue to deepen in the years ahead. He also reiterated the National Press Club’s commitment to providing a platform for meaningful dialogue between diplomats, policymakers and journalists.

headline: IDCPC Minister calls on Field Marshal Asim Munir
description: Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee (IDCPC), Mr Liu Haixing, called on the Chief of Army Staff (COAS)
author: APP
article_text: Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee (IDCPC), Mr Liu Haixing, called on the Chief of Army Staff (COAS) and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, NI (M), HJ, at General Headquarters (GHQ) here on Monday. “During the meeting, both sides discussed matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and international security dynamics, and bilateral relations. They expressed their shared resolve to further strengthen the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Pakistan and China,” said a news release issued by Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR). The COAS highlighted the historic and time-tested bonds between the two countries and emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages and expanded cooperation across areas of mutual interest. The visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership between Pakistan and China.

headline: Senate committee questions FBR over Rs 1,120 bn imports, demands records within two days
description: A Senate Sub-Committee on Interior and Anti-Narcotics has expressed serious concern over the alleged misuse of the FATA/PATA tax exemption scheme, delays in
author: APP
article_text:
A Senate Sub-Committee on Interior and Anti-Narcotics has expressed serious concern over the alleged misuse of the FATA/PATA tax exemption scheme, delays in recovering billions of rupees in outstanding taxes, and the failure of several companies to provide required records.

Convenor Senator Saifullah Abro directed the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and other relevant institutions to submit complete documents, determine potential revenue losses and establish responsibility for any violations of the law.

The meeting was held at Parliament House under the chairmanship of Senator Saifullah Abro. It reviewed the issuance of consumption certificates for imported goods, alleged tax evasion, non-payment of dues, investigations, and the performance of relevant departments.

Senator Umar Farooq and officials from the Interior Ministry, FBR, FIA, police and other departments attended the meeting and briefed the Committee.

During the briefing, officials informed the Committee that imported goods worth approximately Rs1,120 billion under the FATA/PATA tax exemption scheme were under scrutiny. Consumption certificates and related records had been identified for goods worth around Rs389 billion, while further details were required regarding the remaining imports, their utilisation and outstanding tax liabilities.

The Committee was also informed that 223 consumption certificates had been issued to 108 companies. It questioned why complete information about imports, factory production, utilisation of goods and tax payments was unavailable for all companies.

Senator Abro questioned the performance of the FBR, stating that Pakistan was seeking loans from international financial institutions while billions of rupees in alleged tax dues remained unrecovered. He said negligence and delays in collecting taxes were unacceptable.

He declared that public money would be recovered at all costs, adding that national resources belonged to the people and no compromise would be made in protecting them. If investigations established tax evasion or financial irregularities, those responsible must be identified, legal action initiated and outstanding amounts deposited into the national exchequer.

The Convenor directed officials to prepare a separate case file containing import records, customs documents, consumption certificates, tax payments, bank statements and other relevant information. He also sought clarification about the legal basis and supporting documents concerning approximately Rs85 billion and the requirements fulfilled before the release of imported goods.

Officials explained that companies were required to deposit an amount or pay order equivalent to the value of imported goods with customs authorities before their release to factories, subject to prescribed conditions.

Under SRO 2021, documents required for consumption certificates included electricity and gas bills, buyers’ bank statements, business records and employee details.

Senator Abro questioned why these requirements had not been properly verified. He directed officials to present consumption certificates and records of 20 major companies identified during the previous meeting. He also sought correspondence with companies whose certificates had been questioned and explanations for cases where no objections had been raised.

He held the concerned officers and inspectors responsible for examining company documents before issuing certificates and directed that any negligence at any level be identified. All required records were ordered to be submitted within two days.

FBR representative Taqi informed the Committee that suspected cases of fraud or tax non-payment could be selected for audit. He said the department was examining relevant cases and would submit audit findings to determine recoverable amounts.

However, Senator Abro rejected the explanation that audits were underway, demanding details of companies that had submitted records, cases examined and practical steps taken to recover taxes.

Officials further informed the Committee that notices had been issued to 512 companies. Some had submitted complete records, while others had provided partial information. If violations or financial irregularities were established, the responsible individuals and companies must face legal action. Outstanding taxes and penalties must be recovered, while criminal cases should be registered where required.

The Committee also discussed potential revenue losses and tax liabilities estimated at Rs400–500 billion. Senator Abro directed that the amount be determined through verification of records and legal scrutiny.

The relevant authorities were directed to examine import documents, factory records, utilisation of goods and the legal validity of consumption certificates.

Senator Abro directed officials to prepare a comprehensive report by November 9, covering the business activities and import records of five key companies. The report would help the Committee review the matter before the Peshawar High Court proceedings scheduled for November 12, 2026.

He instructed the relevant institutions to coordinate with their legal teams, prepare documentary evidence and submit complete responses before the court.

The Convenor directed officials to provide consumption certificates, import records, notices, court petitions, potential tax liabilities, and correspondence involving relevant officers without delay. He reiterated that the required documents must be submitted within two days and that all investigations and recovery efforts must be completed in accordance with the law.

Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja has stressed the need for responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the judicial system, saying reliable data, digitised court records, strong cybersecurity and human oversight are essential to making justice delivery quicker, more transparent and effective.

Addressing an international conference on AI and the Judiciary in Islamabad on Monday, she said Pakistan had enacted the Digital Nation Pakistan Act to accelerate the country’s digital transformation. The law provides a framework for using technology to modernise governance, the economy and society.

She said the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) had been established under the Act to set standards for digital transformation. Working with the Ministry of Law and Justice, the authority had also developed standards for machine-readable legislation, enabling conventional PDF legal documents to be converted into formats that AI systems can process using authenticated legal data.

The minister stressed that old court records, pending cases, laws and other legal documents needed to be digitised in line with established standards. She said AI could not deliver dependable results when relying on disorganised information and paper-based records.

Appreciating the efforts of the Ministry of Law and Justice, the law minister and the law secretary, Shaza Fatima also acknowledged the judiciary’s cooperation in advancing the digitalisation process.

Outlining progress in modernising the judicial system, she said the National Information Technology Board (NITB) had signed two memoranda of understanding with the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

“An E-Office system has been introduced at the Supreme Court, while digital systems have been deployed to make the administrative affairs of the Supreme Court of Pakistan and the Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan paperless.

She added that significant progress has been achieved in digitizing the Case Management System. A dashboard has been provided to the higher judiciary, and the Case Management System is active, integrated, and interoperable with provincial courts”.

She pointed out that around 2.2 million cases were pending in Pakistan in 2025, adding that even modest gains in efficiency through technology could help reduce the growing backlog.

The minister also highlighted the importance of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), arbitration and mediation. She praised the Ministry of Law and Justice for taking steps to promote these mechanisms as alternatives and support systems to conventional court proceedings.

Discussing the use of AI in legal services, she said Pakistani startups, including Munshi and Lawbot Pakistan, were developing technology-based solutions to help lawyers and members of the public access legal assistance.

However, she cautioned that public trust was essential to the adoption of AI in the justice system. Since large language models can sometimes produce inaccurate or unverified information, she said human oversight must remain an integral part of judicial processes.

She added that effective AI integration required secure and dedicated databases containing verified court judgments, legislation, case law, court records and relevant international legal research. Strong safeguards for cybersecurity, data privacy and accountability would also be necessary.

Shaza Fatima said cooperation between technology developers and legal professionals was equally important. She noted that AI-based legal tools would only meet practical requirements if developers understood the needs of the judiciary and legal practitioners received the necessary AI training.

The minister described the national guidelines on AI use in the judiciary, issued by the National Judicial Policy Committee in April 2026, as a significant development.

Citing UNESCO data presented at the conference, she said only nine per cent of countries worldwide had issued guidelines for the use of AI in their judicial systems. She said this highlighted the need for clear national policies, codes of conduct and regulatory frameworks.

She urged participating countries to share their experiences and best practices and develop national guidelines to ensure the responsible use of AI in judicial systems.

The minister observed that people were increasingly using digital platforms to access healthcare, education, financial services and government facilities, adding that the justice system also needed to keep pace with these changes.

She said technology and AI could bring legal assistance and access to justice closer to citizens, saving time and resources while improving transparency and efficiency.

Reiterating the need for wider training and capacity-building initiatives, she said technology experts must understand legal requirements, while members of the legal profession needed to develop AI-related skills to work together on practical solutions.

In her concluding remarks, Shaza Fatima thanked the IMAC team, the project director, Ministry of Law and Justice, Federal Judicial Academy, Farabi Center for AI and Cybersecurity, Pakistan Digital Authority, NITB and National Center for Artificial Intelligence for their contributions.

Welcoming international delegates to Islamabad, she said cooperation, shared learning and collective efforts could help establish a secure, reliable and interconnected judicial system that benefits countries and their citizens.

headline: Over 15 million people receive Rs27 billion relief under PM Fuel Relief Scheme: Tarar
description: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday said more than 15 million people had so far benefited from the Prime Minister’s
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday said more than 15 million people had so far benefited from the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme, with Rs27 billion disbursed to provide subsidised petroleum products to eligible consumers.

Addressing a press conference here alongside Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, he said the government, on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, had prevented an increase of Rs15 per litre in petrol prices, shifting the additional burden to oil refineries instead of passing it on to consumers.

He said the prime minister’s vision from the outset had been to minimise the financial burden on the people, adding that the refineries would bear an estimated monthly burden of Rs15 billion.

The information minister said the international situation, particularly developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, had put pressure on global economies and energy markets. Pakistan had also been affected by regional developments, but its macroeconomic indicators remained positive, he added.

He said the prime minister had issued clear instructions that the impact of the evolving international situation should not be passed on to the public.

Describing the fuel relief initiative as a major public welfare measure, Tarar said the scheme provided petrol at subsidised rates to motorcycles, Qingqi rickshaws and vehicles with engine capacity of up to 800cc.

He said more than 15 million registrations had been completed under the scheme, while approximately Rs27 billion had so far been disbursed as relief. Payments were also being made to petrol pumps for fuel supplied at subsidised rates, he added.

The minister said the initiative had been made possible through coordinated efforts by the Ministry of Information Technology, Ministry of Petroleum, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) and State Bank of Pakistan.

He said the scheme had been successfully launched across the country and would continue to facilitate eligible consumers.

Responding to questions, Tarar said there was no shortage of essential commodities in the country, adding that cargo arrivals and supply chains had been maintained even under challenging circumstances to meet national requirements.

He urged the public to avoid speculation and refrain from believing unverified reports and rumours.

Commenting on the development situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the minister said the province had been neglected during PTI’s 13-and-a-half-year rule, particularly in infrastructure development and public welfare.

He said the provincial government had failed to undertake significant projects involving roads, bridges, hospitals, colleges and universities, while the youth had also been deprived of laptop distribution initiatives.

Referring to his recent visit to Kohat, Tarar said the motorway and Kohat Tunnel had been constructed during the PML-N government, questioning why subsequent provincial governments had failed to establish projects such as a Safe City system, a kidney and liver transplant centre and new universities.

He said laptops could also have been distributed among young people to facilitate their education and professional development.

The minister said Islamabad and Punjab were bearing a substantial burden, while alleging that PTI had attempted to undermine Pakistan’s economy by writing letters to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to push the country out of its programme.

He said the performance of successive governments could be assessed through key economic indicators, including foreign exchange reserves, debt repayments, macroeconomic performance and economic stability.

Tarar said the incumbent government had introduced comprehensive reforms to stabilise the economy and put it on a path of sustainable development.

He said Pakistan came first and political parties and their leaders came afterwards, adding that there could be no justification for placing any political leader above the country.

Highlighting the government’s tax reforms, he said the PML-N government had initiated structural reforms in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), while technology-based monitoring of manufacturing processes had enabled the collection of additional revenue.

He said an additional Rs60 billion in taxes had been collected from the sugar industry alone.

He added that technology had also been introduced in the cement, tobacco and beverages sectors to monitor production and establish traceability mechanisms, while structural reforms had been undertaken within the FBR.

The minister said reforms had also been introduced in the ports and shipping sectors, including a fee appraisal system at ports.

He said the government had taken several reform measures despite challenging economic circumstances, describing its achievements in stabilising the economy as significant.

Criticising the previous government, Tarar said those who had come to power with the slogan of change had left the country facing serious economic challenges.

He questioned the previous government’s economic achievements, saying its leadership had demonstrated a lack of understanding of the exchange-rate mechanism.

He said that the previous government had attempted to derail efforts towards economic stability and had encouraged a civil disobedience movement, urging people to burn electricity bills and withhold payments.

The information minister further noted that the PTI government had allowed millions of non-customs-paid (NCP) vehicles to operate in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Referring again to his Kohat visit, he said he had not seen even a single registered motorcycle there, questioning whether vehicle registration and revenue collection were not the responsibility of the provincial government.

He said the revenue generated through proper registration could have been utilised for public welfare.

Tarar said the previous rulers had misled the people through slogans without delivering tangible results, and challenged them to identify notable achievements of their economic team.

Commenting on the OGRA chairman, he said the authority was being regulated effectively, and the results of sound policies were becoming visible. He added that the chairman had previously been part of the prime minister’s team and would continue to serve with it.

article_html:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday said more than 15 million people had so far benefited from the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme, with Rs27 billion disbursed to provide subsidised petroleum products to eligible consumers.

Addressing a press conference here alongside Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, he said the government, on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, had prevented an increase of Rs15 per litre in petrol prices, shifting the additional burden to oil refineries instead of passing it on to consumers.

Al-Shifa Trust to organize free eye surgical camp

He said the prime minister’s vision from the outset had been to minimise the financial burden on the people, adding that the refineries would bear an estimated monthly burden of Rs15 billion.

The information minister said the international situation, particularly developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, had put pressure on global economies and energy markets. Pakistan had also been affected by regional developments, but its macroeconomic indicators remained positive, he added.

He said the prime minister had issued clear instructions that the impact of the evolving international situation should not be passed on to the public.

Direct flights imperative to give quantum jump to Pak-Spanish bilateral trade: Carlos Aragon

Describing the fuel relief initiative as a major public welfare measure, Tarar said the scheme provided petrol at subsidised rates to motorcycles, Qingqi rickshaws and vehicles with engine capacity of up to 800cc.

He said more than 15 million registrations had been completed under the scheme, while approximately Rs27 billion had so far been disbursed as relief. Payments were also being made to petrol pumps for fuel supplied at subsidised rates, he added.

The minister said the initiative had been made possible through coordinated efforts by the Ministry of Information Technology, Ministry of Petroleum, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) and State Bank of Pakistan.

ECP says 1,847 nomination papers issued for Islamabad LG polls over weekend

He said the scheme had been successfully launched across the country and would continue to facilitate eligible consumers.

Responding to questions, Tarar said there was no shortage of essential commodities in the country, adding that cargo arrivals and supply chains had been maintained even under challenging circumstances to meet national requirements.

He urged the public to avoid speculation and refrain from believing unverified reports and rumours.

Commenting on the development situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the minister said the province had been neglected during PTI’s 13-and-a-half-year rule, particularly in infrastructure development and public welfare.

Salman Safdar meets Imran Khan after seven months; PTI forms committee on jail access

He said the provincial government had failed to undertake significant projects involving roads, bridges, hospitals, colleges and universities, while the youth had also been deprived of laptop distribution initiatives.

Referring to his recent visit to Kohat, Tarar said the motorway and Kohat Tunnel had been constructed during the PML-N government, questioning why subsequent provincial governments had failed to establish projects such as a Safe City system, a kidney and liver transplant centre and new universities.

He said laptops could also have been distributed among young people to facilitate their education and professional development.

Petrol price cut by Rs3.40 per litre, diesel by Rs7.76

The minister said Islamabad and Punjab were bearing a substantial burden, while alleging that PTI had attempted to undermine Pakistan’s economy by writing letters to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to push the country out of its programme.

He said the performance of successive governments could be assessed through key economic indicators, including foreign exchange reserves, debt repayments, macroeconomic performance and economic stability.

Tarar said the incumbent government had introduced comprehensive reforms to stabilise the economy and put it on a path of sustainable development.

He said Pakistan came first and political parties and their leaders came afterwards, adding that there could be no justification for placing any political leader above the country.

Highlighting the government’s tax reforms, he said the PML-N government had initiated structural reforms in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), while technology-based monitoring of manufacturing processes had enabled the collection of additional revenue.

He said an additional Rs60 billion in taxes had been collected from the sugar industry alone.

He added that technology had also been introduced in the cement, tobacco and beverages sectors to monitor production and establish traceability mechanisms, while structural reforms had been undertaken within the FBR.

The minister said reforms had also been introduced in the ports and shipping sectors, including a fee appraisal system at ports.

He said the government had taken several reform measures despite challenging economic circumstances, describing its achievements in stabilising the economy as significant.

Criticising the previous government, Tarar said those who had come to power with the slogan of change had left the country facing serious economic challenges.

He questioned the previous government’s economic achievements, saying its leadership had demonstrated a lack of understanding of the exchange-rate mechanism.

He said that the previous government had attempted to derail efforts towards economic stability and had encouraged a civil disobedience movement, urging people to burn electricity bills and withhold payments.

The information minister further noted that the PTI government had allowed millions of non-customs-paid (NCP) vehicles to operate in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Referring again to his Kohat visit, he said he had not seen even a single registered motorcycle there, questioning whether vehicle registration and revenue collection were not the responsibility of the provincial government.

He said the revenue generated through proper registration could have been utilised for public welfare.

Tarar said the previous rulers had misled the people through slogans without delivering tangible results, and challenged them to identify notable achievements of their economic team.

Commenting on the OGRA chairman, he said the authority was being regulated effectively, and the results of sound policies were becoming visible. He added that the chairman had previously been part of the prime minister’s team and would continue to serve with it.

headline: Dry weather expected across most parts of country on Tuesday: PMD
description: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast dry weather across most parts of the country on Tuesday, with cold conditions during the morning and
author: APP
article_text:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast dry weather across most parts of the country on Tuesday, with cold conditions during the morning and night in northern areas, while isolated light rain and light snowfall over hills are likely in upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan.

According to the weather forecast issued by the Pakistan Meteorological Department on Monday, Islamabad and its surroundings are expected to experience dry weather, with cool conditions during morning and night.

In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, most districts are likely to remain dry, while partly cloudy skies and cold conditions are expected in hilly areas.

Light rain accompanied by thunderstorms may occur at isolated places in Chitral, Dir, Swat, Kohistan and Kurram. Light rain is also expected in Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat and adjoining areas during the night.

Most districts of Punjab are likely to experience dry weather. However, shallow fog or smog may develop in Lahore, Faisalabad, Multan, Gujranwala, Narowal, Sialkot and adjoining areas during morning hours. Murree, Galiyat and surrounding areas are expected to remain partly cloudy, with cold conditions during morning and night.

In Sindh, dry weather is expected in most districts, while southern parts of the province are likely to experience hot conditions during the daytime.

Most districts of Balochistan are also expected to remain dry, with cold conditions in northern areas during the morning and night. However, cloudy weather with light rain accompanied by thunderstorms is likely in Chaman, Pishin, Zhob, Qilla Abdullah, Quetta and adjoining areas.

Partly cloudy and cold weather is expected in Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan. Isolated places in Gilgit-Baltistan may receive light rain accompanied by thunderstorms, with light snowfall over the hills.

During the past 24 hours, dry weather prevailed over most parts of the country, while northern areas remained cold and partly cloudy. Isolated rainfall was recorded in upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with Mir Khani receiving 5 millimetres, Drosh 3 mm, Lower Dir 2 mm, Upper Dir 1 mm and Kalam 2 mm.

Leh recorded the lowest minimum temperature at minus 2 degrees Celsius, followed by Babusar at 2 degrees Celsius. The minimum and maximum temperatures recorded in major cities were: Islamabad 12/28C, Lahore 16/30C, Karachi 23/35C, Peshawar 15/29C, Quetta 6/26C, Gilgit 7/22C, Muzaffarabad 11/28C, Skardu 4/17C, Murree 6/19C, Faisalabad 17/30C and Multan 18/31C.

In the adjoining region, Srinagar recorded 5/23C, Jammu 16/29C, Leh minus 2/12C, Pulwama 4/22C, Anantnag 3/24C, Shopian 4/23C and Baramulla 3/22C.

headline: HSA opens admissions for postgraduate diploma in health research
description: The Health Services Academy (HSA) has announced admissions to its Postgraduate Diploma in Health Research, providing healthcare professionals and graduates
author: APP
article_text:
The Health Services Academy (HSA) has announced admissions to its Postgraduate Diploma in Health Research, providing healthcare professionals and graduates from relevant fields an opportunity to develop their research and academic capabilities.

The two-semester programme will be offered in a hybrid format, combining online classes with in-person learning.

Graduates holding degrees in MBBS, BDS, Allied Health Sciences, BS Nursing, Social Sciences and other relevant disciplines are eligible to apply.

The deadline for registration and fee submission is November 7, 2026, while classes are scheduled to begin on November 11.

The diploma is designed to equip participants with advanced research skills, enabling them to plan and conduct educational research, improve their academic writing and effectively share research findings.

headline: Main suspect arrested in killing of four family members in Skardu
description: Police have arrested the main suspect, identified as Rajab, along with an alleged accomplice in the killing of four members of a family in Skardu, while raids
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Police have arrested the main suspect, identified as Rajab, along with an alleged accomplice in the killing of four members of a family in Skardu, while raids are underway to apprehend the remaining suspects.

According to police, those allegedly involved in the killings had fled to Kurram district to evade arrest.

Investigators have also gathered evidence indicating that five people may have been involved in the murders, police said.

The victims were identified as Muhammad Aslam, his wife Hania Aslam, their four-year-old son Mehdi and two-year-old daughter Zahra. The family was found dead inside their home in Madina Colony, Skardu.

Police said the victims were attacked with sharp-edged weapons after the suspects entered the house.

The couple had married for love in Karachi around six years ago before relocating to Skardu. Aslam was a native of Skardu, while his wife belonged to Parachinar.

A case was registered on the complaint of Khadim Hussain, the deceased man's brother. The FIR nominated the woman's father, brothers and maternal uncle as suspects.

The complainant told police that Aslam had previously received serious threats over his marriage.

Earlier, DIG Gilgit-Baltistan Asif Mehmood said investigators were examining all possible aspects of the incident, including whether the killings were linked to the couple's marriage.

He assured that all available resources would be used to arrest those responsible and ensure justice for the victims.

The killings triggered protests in Skardu, where residents called for the immediate arrest of the suspects and justice for the family.

headline: PHP police arrest 60 wanted criminals
description: FAISALABAD -The Punjab Highway Patrol (PHP) Police on Sunday intensified its crackdown against criminal elements in Faisalabad region during October
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: FAISALABAD -The Punjab Highway Patrol (PHP) Police on Sunday intensified its crackdown against criminal elements in Faisalabad region during October 2026,arresting 38 proclaimed offenders and 22 court absconders,recovering 599 liters of liquor and safely reuniting seven missing children with their families. According to SP Punjab Highway Patrol Faisalabad Region Muhammad Tariq Malik,the force registered 692 cases during the month as part of its efforts to maintain law and order,prevent crime,ensure highway safety and provide timely assistance to commuters. He said Faisalabad district accounted for 271 cases,followed by Jhang with 213,Toba Tek Singh 135 and Chiniot 73. During operations against criminal elements, PHP personnel arrested 60 wanted suspects,including 38 proclaimed offenders and 22 court absconders. In its drive against drug-related offenses,the force registered 34 cases and recovered 599 liters of liquor to curb illegal activities and prevent the circulation of intoxicating substances in the region,he added.The PHP also intensified action against illegal weapons,registering five cases and recovering three 30-bore pistols, one 12-bore gun and 12 rounds and cartridges. In other recoveries,the force seized a stolen motorcycle bearing registration number ARR-9274 and cash amounting to Rs.21,100. During a separate operation in Faisalabad district,PHP personnel also confiscated 595 kilograms of hazardous meat from dead animals,preventing its potential supply to consumers. Alongside law enforcement operations,the force continued providing public assistance and emergency support to highway users. Malik said PHP personnel assisted 2,091 people across the region by providing guidance and timely help to commuters facing difficulties during their journeys. To ensure smooth traffic flow and improve road safety, the personnel also removed 61 encroachments from highways,facilitating motorists and helping ensure safer movement of traffic. In a significant humanitarian initiative,the force recovered seven missing children from different locations and safely reunited them with their parents and relatives. Reviewing the monthly performance,SP Muhammad Tariq Malik said the Punjab Highway Patrol Faisalabad Region was diligently performing its professional responsibilities to prevent crime on highways,protect the lives and property of citizens and provide commuters with a safe,secure and peaceful travelling environment. He reaffirmed that the force would continue its operations against criminal elements while maintaining its focus on public safety,highway security and timely assistance to road users. He added that public service and protection of citizens would remain a priority with patrol personnel continuing to utilize their professional capabilities to ensure safer highways and improved security throughout Faisalabad region.

According to SP Punjab Highway Patrol Faisalabad Region Muhammad Tariq Malik,the force registered 692 cases during the month as part of its efforts to maintain law and order,prevent crime,ensure highway safety and provide timely assistance to commuters. He said Faisalabad district accounted for 271 cases,followed by Jhang with 213,Toba Tek Singh 135 and Chiniot 73. During operations against criminal elements, PHP personnel arrested 60 wanted suspects,including 38 proclaimed offenders and 22 court absconders. In its drive against drug-related offenses,the force registered 34 cases and recovered 599 liters of liquor to curb illegal activities and prevent the circulation of intoxicating substances in the region,he added.The PHP also intensified action against illegal weapons,registering five cases and recovering three 30-bore pistols, one 12-bore gun and 12 rounds and cartridges.
In other recoveries,the force seized a stolen motorcycle bearing registration number ARR-9274 and cash amounting to Rs.21,100.
During a separate operation in Faisalabad district,PHP personnel also confiscated 595 kilograms of hazardous meat from dead animals,preventing its potential supply to consumers.
Alongside law enforcement operations,the force continued providing public assistance and emergency support to highway users. 
Malik said PHP personnel assisted 2,091 people across the region by providing guidance and timely help to commuters facing difficulties during their journeys.
To ensure smooth traffic flow and improve road safety, the personnel also removed 61 encroachments from highways,facilitating motorists and helping ensure safer movement of traffic.
In a significant humanitarian initiative,the force recovered seven missing children from different locations and safely reunited them with their parents and relatives.
Reviewing the monthly performance,SP Muhammad Tariq Malik said the Punjab Highway Patrol Faisalabad Region was diligently performing its professional responsibilities to prevent crime on highways,protect the lives and property of citizens and provide commuters with a safe,secure and peaceful travelling environment.
He reaffirmed that the force would continue its operations against criminal elements while maintaining its focus on public safety,highway security and timely assistance to road users.
He added that public service and protection of citizens would remain a priority with patrol personnel continuing to utilize their professional capabilities to ensure safer highways and improved security throughout Faisalabad region.

headline: Farewell ceremony held in honour of two transferred DSPs in Muzaffargarh
description: MUZAFFARGARH - District Police Officer (DPO) Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah hosted a farewell ceremony in honour of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) City Circle
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: MUZAFFARGARH - District Police Officer (DPO) Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah hosted a farewell ceremony in honour of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) City Circle Zafar Wattoo and DSP Alipur Circle Allah Yar Saifi, who have been transferred from Muzaffargarh district. According to Police Media Coordinator Nawab Umar Khan Sherwani, the ceremony was attended by DPO Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah, SP Investigation Nasir Mahmood and ASP Nabeel Ahmed Langrial. DSPs from across the district, heads of various branches, DSP Investigation Malik Akbar Mahmood, DSP Safe City Tariq Sattar and his staff were also present. During the ceremony, the DPO presented honorary shields to both outgoing officers in recognition of their professional services and contributions to the district. He also extended his best wishes to them for their new assignments.

headline: Faisalabad police arrest thousands of suspects in major crime crackdown
description: FAISALABAD - Under the leadership of City Police Officer (CPO) Tanveer Hussain, Faisalabad Police have arrested thousands of suspects involved in serious
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: FAISALABAD - Under the leadership of City Police Officer (CPO) Tanveer Hussain, Faisalabad Police have arrested thousands of suspects involved in serious criminal activities during the current year. According to police, a total of 434 suspects involved in murder cases have been arrested and sent to jail during the current year. Furthermore 43 suspects involved in blind murder cases were traced and arrested with the help of modern technical resources. Police also arrested 691 suspects involved in attempted murder cases, while 75 suspects wanted in robbery cases were apprehended and legal proceedings were initiated against them. In addition 3,380 suspects involved in street robbery incidents were arrested as part of the ongoing crackdown against criminal elements. Police officials stated that modern technology and technical resources are being utilized to trace and apprehend suspects involved in serious criminal activities. CPO Faisalabad Tanveer Hussain stated that all legal requirements would be fulfilled to ensure that suspects involved in serious crimes receive punishment in accordance with the law.

headline: Khawaja Farid University, college face decline amid mismanagement
description: RAHIM YAR KHAN - Two major educational institutions named after renowned regional Sufi saint Khawaja Ghulam Farid are reportedly losing their academic standing
author: IHSAN UL HAQ
article_text:
RAHIM YAR KHAN - Two major educational institutions named after renowned regional Sufi saint Khawaja Ghulam Farid are reportedly losing their academic standing amid prolonged mismanagement, internal politics and the absence of permanent heads, forcing students to seek quality education in other major cities. Khawaja Farid College, established in 1952 as the first college in the district, and Khawaja Farid University, established in 2014 as its first university, were both named after the celebrated saint. However, residents say both institutions have witnessed a steady decline in academic standards due to alleged favouritism in appointments and administrative affairs. The university, established during the tenure of former chief minister Shehbaz Sharif, has allegedly been operating under ad hoc arrangements even 12 years after its establishment. Key positions, including registrar, controller of examinations and treasurer, have reportedly not been filled on a permanent basis. The prolonged absence of a permanent controller of examinations has caused serious difficulties for students, particularly delays in degree verification. According to reports, some students have even lost foreign scholarship opportunities as a result. Successive vice chancellors have also been accused of appointing people from their own groups to key positions. The university is reportedly facing a shortage of faculty members, including the absence of a pro-vice chancellor, affecting its academic and administrative affairs. Allegations have also surfaced that classes were launched in certain departments without proper approval for faculty positions and new disciplines during the tenures of its first two vice chancellors, damaging the institution’s reputation. Former vice chancellors have also faced allegations of making appointments in violation of merit and awarding contracts to favoured individuals, compromising the quality of construction work. Around three years ago, a newly constructed building on the campus reportedly collapsed shortly after its completion, allegedly due to substandard construction. However, no action was reportedly taken against those responsible. The university’s international ranking has also allegedly declined sharply. The vice chancellor appointed around two years ago reportedly attempted to address these problems but could not overcome powerful internal lobbies and administrative differences. He resigned a few days ago, citing personal reasons. In 2022, a principal was removed following a written complaint against a teacher who allegedly used inappropriate language. The college subsequently remained under acting principals for three years. In February 2025, a newly appointed principal reportedly lost his position following a controversy involving the showering of currency notes on female performers during a welcome party.

His successor was also reportedly removed over allegations, leaving the college once again under an acting principal. Citizens have appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Governor Sardar Saleem Haider to appoint permanent heads of both institutions without further delay. They called for the appointment of capable administrators committed to merit, transparency and institutional reforms to restore the lost prestige of the university and college and prevent students from having to move to other cities for quality education.

Around three years ago, a newly constructed building on the campus reportedly collapsed shortly after its completion, allegedly due to substandard construction. However, no action was reportedly taken against those responsible. The university’s international ranking has also allegedly declined sharply. The vice chancellor appointed around two years ago reportedly attempted to address these problems but could not overcome powerful internal lobbies and administrative differences. He resigned a few days ago, citing personal reasons. In 2022, a principal was removed following a written complaint against a teacher who allegedly used inappropriate language. The college subsequently remained under acting principals for three years.

In February 2025, a newly appointed principal reportedly lost his position following a controversy involving the showering of currency notes on female performers during a welcome party.

His successor was also reportedly removed over allegations, leaving the college once again under an acting principal.

Citizens have appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Governor Sardar Saleem Haider to appoint permanent heads of both institutions without further delay. They called for the appointment of capable administrators committed to merit, transparency and institutional reforms to restore the lost prestige of the university and college and prevent students from having to move to other cities for quality education.

headline: FIC schedules live cardiac surgeries during PHC inspection
description: FAISALABAD - The administration of Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology (FIC) has adopted an unusual approach by scheduling live cardiac surgeries from the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
FAISALABAD - The administration of Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology (FIC) has adopted an unusual approach by scheduling live cardiac surgeries from the hospital’s operation theatres for participants attending a PACVTS conference during the period of Punjab Healthcare Commission inspections, raising questions about the arrangement. The FIC Medical Superintendent Dr. Nadeem Akhtar issued an official order (No.30419-25) on October 29, 2026, stating that teams from the Punjab Healthcare Commission (PHC) would conduct inspections at the hospital from November 2 to November 7, 2026. In this regard all heads of departments, doctors, nurses, paramedical staff and other employees were directed to perform their duties according to their respective duty rosters, avoid negligence in their work and refrain from taking leave. The order further stated that strict departmental action would be taken against those who failed to comply with the instructions. On the other hand a two day cardiac surgery conference is being organised at a private hotel by the Pakistan Association of Cardiovascular Surgeons in collaboration with FIC. According to the conference programme, live cardiac surgeries will be broadcast directly from FIC’s operation theatres to participants at the private hotel on Friday 06, November from 8:30 am to 12:30 pm so that young and newly doctors can benefit as much as possible from the professional experience of senior doctors.

However according to the order issued by the MS PHC inspection teams will examine staff attendance, hospital records, emergency services, routine operations and other related matters. Under these circumstances it would become difficult for the operation theatre, anaesthesia, perfusion, nursing and other relevant staff to arrange live surgeries during the inspections. As a result hospital staff is reportedly concerned over the arrangement. When FIC MS Dr Nadeem Akhtar was contacted for his comments on the matter, he stated contrary to the inspection period mentioned in his own official order, that the PHC teams would visit the hospital from November 2 to November 5, while live surgeries would be shown to conference participants on November 6.

headline: Man kills former mother-in-law over divorce dispute
description: Mailsi - A woman was killed and a man critically injured when her former son-in-law, along with his accomplices, allegedly stormed a house and opened fire over
author: Peer Abdul Razaq Qureshi
article_text: Mailsi - A woman was killed and a man critically injured when her former son-in-law, along with his accomplices, allegedly stormed a house and opened fire over a divorce dispute in Chak No. 204/WB, within the jurisdiction of Tibba Sultanpur Police Station. The deceased was identified as Amina Bibi, while Ghulam Shabbir sustained serious injuries and was shifted to Nishtar Hospital Multan in critical condition. According to police, the incident occurred near Danish School, where accused Naveed Iqbal, accompanied by Muhammad Shahbaz and another unidentified person, allegedly entered the house under the cover of darkness and opened indiscriminate fire. The complainant, Muhammad Rafaqat, son of the deceased, told police that his sister was previously married to Naveed Iqbal but the couple had subsequently divorced. He alleged that the accused, along with his accomplices, entered their house over the divorce dispute and shot his mother dead. Following the incident, Tibba Sultanpur police reached the scene, took the body into custody and initiated legal proceedings. SHO Rana Saqib Nazir said a case had been registered on the complainant’s application and raids were being conducted to arrest the nominated suspects. He added that all aspects of the incident were being investigated.

headline: DIG Prisons inspects Bahawalnagar District Jail
description: BAHAWALNAGAR - DIG Prisons Qazi Muhammad Aslam visited District Jail Bahawalnagar and inspected various departments to review facilities provided to inmates,
author: Ali Raza
article_text: BAHAWALNAGAR - DIG Prisons Qazi Muhammad Aslam visited District Jail Bahawalnagar and inspected various departments to review facilities provided to inmates, security arrangements and administrative affairs. Accompanied by Superintendent District Jail Bahawalnagar Syed Hassan Mujtaba, the DIG conducted a detailed inspection of the jail hospital, kitchen, visitors’ shed and other sections. He reviewed cleanliness, food quality, medical facilities, security arrangements and the overall conditions of prisoners. Speaking on the occasion, Qazi Muhammad Aslam said providing the best possible facilities to prisoners was a top priority under the special instructions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif and Inspector General Prisons. He said all available resources were being utilised to ensure proper cleanliness, quality food, medical facilities and effective security arrangements in prisons. He added that treating prisoners humanely and in accordance with the law was a fundamental responsibility of the jail administration. The DIG expressed satisfaction with the administrative affairs and arrangements of various departments at District Jail Bahawalnagar and appreciated the efforts of the jail administration.

headline: False rape cases emerge as new challenge for south Punjab police
description: MUZAFFARGARH - Allegations of the misuse of stringent anti-rape laws to implicate rivals in fabricated cases are emerging as a new challenge for law
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text: MUZAFFARGARH - Allegations of the misuse of stringent anti-rape laws to implicate rivals in fabricated cases are emerging as a new challenge for law enforcement agencies across South Punjab, with a growing number of complaints raising concerns about the credibility of criminal proceedings and the protection of genuine victims. Police records indicate that Muzaffargarh reported the highest number of allegedly fabricated cases among major cities in South Punjab last month, with 27 such cases reported. In October alone, 11 FIRs were reportedly registered in attempts to implicate individuals in false rape cases. Lodhran recorded six similar cases, according to available figures. In a separate development in Multan, an allegation of sexual assault reportedly made after a woman returned from a birthday celebration was also found to be false during the subsequent proceedings, according to police sources. Meanwhile, legal proceedings have been initiated against four individuals, including two women, in Muzaffargarh over allegations of filing false cases. Police have invoked provisions of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021, and initiated further legal action, including proceedings for penalties where applicable. The first such cases in the area were reportedly registered at Sanawan Police Station, within Sanawan police circle, followed by another case in Qasba Gujrat. In one of the cases, FIR No. 288/26 was registered on the complaint of a woman identified as Bakhtu against a man named Jumma on allegations of rape. Police said the complainant subsequently made a statement before a court in favour of the accused and expressed willingness to compromise. A subsequent review of police records reportedly raised questions about similar complaints allegedly lodged by the woman at different police stations, followed by statements that benefited the nominated accused. Following the review, the SHO of Qasba Gujrat Police Station and SDPO Sanawan Malik Akbar initiated legal proceedings under the Anti-Rape Act 2021. Police case No. 625/26 was reportedly registered at Sanawan Police Station under Sections 22(2)(a) and 22(2)(b) of the Act. The reported action by SDPO Malik Akbar has been welcomed by political, social, business and civil society representatives in Qasba Gujrat, who described the move as an important step towards preventing the misuse of legal provisions and strengthening public confidence in the justice system. They stressed that stringent laws intended to protect women and children must not be exploited to settle personal scores or target opponents. At the same time, they emphasised that genuine survivors of sexual violence must receive protection, dignity and timely justice. The representatives called for impartial investigations, evidence-based prosecutions and strict adherence to due process, saying that accountability must extend to anyone found guilty of deliberately filing fabricated complaints. They also praised SDPO Malik Akbar’s reported initiative, urging law enforcement authorities to ensure that the law is applied without fear or favour across Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu and Layyah. The allegations of false reporting remain subject to independent investigation and judicial determination. Registration of a case does not, by itself, establish guilt.
