headline: Why Nations Move Forward and Why We Are Left Behind - A Blueprint for Pakistan's Revival
description: When we look at the world's major powers, one reality becomes very clear. Nations do not progress by chance, they progress by the system that governs them.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
When we look at the world's major powers, one reality becomes very clear. Nations do not progress by chance, they progress by the system that governs them.

The United States is run by lawyers and its strength is its institutions. Its constitution is supreme. Every contract is enforceable, every investor is protected, and every citizen knows that the law, not an individual, is final. This legal certainty is why the world invests in America, why innovation thrives in Silicon Valley, and why its economy remains resilient despite political divisions. Their system is designed to outlive any single leader.

China is run by engineers and technocrats. Its strength is long-term planning and ruthless execution. When China decides to build a dam, a port, or a high-speed rail network, it plans for the next 30 to 50 years and it delivers. Its leadership, mostly with backgrounds in engineering and science, focuses on productivity, infrastructure, and industrial growth. In four decades, it lifted over 800 million people out of poverty not by slogans, but by measurable, engineered growth. Their question is never who will get the credit, but whether the project will get completed.

India is run by politicians, but its strength is democratic continuity and economic scale. Despite immense diversity and poverty, India has never compromised on the continuity of its democratic system. It has built strong institutions like its Election Commission, Supreme Court, and Reserve Bank. It has empowered its private sector, invested heavily in IT education, and leveraged its global diaspora. Its politics is noisy, but its economic direction has largely remained consistent, which builds investor confidence.

And then there is Pakistan. Pakistan is a nation of extraordinary potential but with a governance model that has failed to harness it.

Our strengths are undeniable. We are the fifth-largest population in the world with 60 percent youth. We have one of the most fertile lands, vast mineral resources from Thar to Reko Diq, a 1,000 km coastline at the heart of global trade routes, and one of the most generous and hardworking diasporas in the world that sends over 30 billion dollars annually. Our people are resilient. They survive crises, inflation, and uncertainty, and still hope.

But our weaknesses have neutralized our strengths. First, we have institutional fragility. Institutions are often weaker than individuals, and policies change with governments. Second, we have a severe deficit of technocracy. Critical ministries and state-owned enterprises are often led by individuals without domain expertise, resulting in circular debt, failed PIA and Steel Mills, and a stagnant tax base. Third, we have neglected human capital. Our education spending remains below 2 percent of GDP, out-of-school children are over 26 million, and our universities produce degrees but not skills relevant to the global market. Fourth, we have a short-term political economy. We focus on subsidies and short-term relief packages for electoral gains rather than structural reforms in energy, taxation, and exports.

This is why we face recurring crises. While others plan for decades, we plan for the next election. While others protect contracts, we renegotiate them. While others invest in skills, we invest in slogans.

The way forward is not a mystery. It requires three fundamental shifts.

One, the shift from personality to institution. We need to make our institutions, particularly judiciary, civil service, and regulatory bodies, truly independent, merit-based, and empowered. Rule of law must be uniform and predictable. This alone will bring investment and trust.

Two, the shift from generalist rule to expert led governance. Pakistan needs a new governance model where politicians set the national vision but technocrats, engineers, economists, scientists, and IT experts execute it. We need to place CEOs on merit in state enterprises, empower a professional civil service, and create a National Economic Council with a 20-year mandate that cannot be overturned by any single government.

Three, the shift from consumption to production. We must radically reform our economy. This means documenting the economy to expand our tax base, fixing our energy sector by moving to renewable and local resources, investing at least 4 percent of GDP in education with a focus on technical and vocational training, and providing cheap credit and ease of doing business to our small and medium industries which are the real engine of jobs.

Finally, we need continuity of policy. Let political governments change, but let Pakistan's economic and educational roadmap continue.

Pakistan is not a poor country. It is a poorly managed rich country. The moment we replace a system of patronage with a system of merit, and a politics of short-term survival with a vision of long-term national interest, no power on earth can stop Pakistan from rising.

Their system is designed to outlive any single leader.

China is run by engineers and technocrats. Its strength is long-term planning and ruthless execution. When China decides to build a dam, a port, or a high-speed rail network, it plans for the next 30 to 50 years and it delivers. Its leadership, mostly with backgrounds in engineering and science, focuses on productivity, infrastructure, and industrial growth. In four decades, it lifted over 800 million people out of poverty not by slogans, but by measurable, engineered growth. Their question is never who will get the credit, but whether the project will get completed.

India is run by politicians, but its strength is democratic continuity and economic scale. Despite immense diversity and poverty, India has never compromised on the continuity of its democratic system. It has built strong institutions like its Election Commission, Supreme Court, and Reserve Bank. It has empowered its private sector, invested heavily in IT education, and leveraged its global diaspora. Its politics is noisy, but its economic direction has largely remained consistent, which builds investor confidence.
And then there is Pakistan. Pakistan is a nation of extraordinary potential but with a governance model that has failed to harness it.

Our strengths are undeniable. We are the fifth-largest population in the world with 60 percent youth. We have one of the most fertile lands, vast mineral resources from Thar to Reko Diq, a 1,000 km coastline at the heart of global trade routes, and one of the most generous and hardworking diasporas in the world that sends over 30 billion dollars annually. Our people are resilient. They survive crises, inflation, and uncertainty, and still hope.

But our weaknesses have neutralized our strengths. First, we have institutional fragility. Institutions are often weaker than individuals, and policies change with governments. Second, we have a severe deficit of technocracy. Critical ministries and state-owned enterprises are often led by individuals without domain expertise, resulting in circular debt, failed PIA and Steel Mills, and a stagnant tax base. Third, we have neglected human capital. Our education spending remains below 2 percent of GDP, out-of-school children are over 26 million, and our universities produce degrees but not skills relevant to the global market. Fourth, we have a short-term political economy. We focus on subsidies and short-term relief packages for electoral gains rather than structural reforms in energy, taxation, and exports.

This is why we face recurring crises. While others plan for decades, we plan for the next election. While others protect contracts, we renegotiate them. While others invest in skills, we invest in slogans.
The way forward is not a mystery. It requires three fundamental shifts.

One, the shift from personality to institution. We need to make our institutions, particularly judiciary, civil service, and regulatory bodies, truly independent, merit-based, and empowered. Rule of law must be uniform and predictable. This alone will bring investment and trust.

Two, the shift from generalist rule to expert led governance. Pakistan needs a new governance model where politicians set the national vision but technocrats, engineers, economists, scientists, and IT experts execute it. We need to place CEOs on merit in state enterprises, empower a professional civil service, and create a National Economic Council with a 20-year mandate that cannot be overturned by any single government.

Three, the shift from consumption to production. We must radically reform our economy. This means documenting the economy to expand our tax base, fixing our energy sector by moving to renewable and local resources, investing at least 4 percent of GDP in education with a focus on technical and vocational training, and providing cheap credit and ease of doing business to our small and medium industries which are the real engine of jobs.
Finally, we need continuity of policy. Let political governments change, but let Pakistan's economic and educational roadmap continue.

Pakistan is not a poor country. It is a poorly managed rich country. The moment we replace a system of patronage with a system of merit, and a politics of short-term survival with a vision of long-term national interest, no power on earth can stop Pakistan from rising.

headline: Sarsabz Farmers Claim All Three Provincial Titles in Punjab's Wheat Yield Competition 2025-26
description: Fatima Fertilizer celebrated farmers’ outstanding achievements at the Sarsabz Ki Jeet Wheat Yield Competition Prize Distribution Ceremony. Farmers using
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Fatima Fertilizer celebrated farmers’ outstanding achievements at the Sarsabz Ki Jeet Wheat Yield Competition Prize Distribution Ceremony. Farmers using Sarsabz Nitrophos and Calcium Ammonium Nitrate (CAN) secured the top three positions at the provincial level and 119 out of 120 district-level positions in the Punjab Wheat Yield Competition 2025–26, announced by the Government of Punjab. Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research, Mr. Rana Tanveer Hussain, addressed the ceremony virtually. The event was also attended by Additional Chief Secretary (ACS), Punjab, Mr. Iftikhar Ali Sahoo ; Secretary Agriculture, Punjab, Mr. Shakeel Ahmad Mian and President, Pakistan Kissan Ittehad, Mr. Khalid Khokhar among other dignitaries.

Sarsabz farmers secured first position in 39 out of 40 districts and claimed all three provincial positions. Mr. Sajjad Hussain from Muzaffargarh secured first provincial position with a yield of 69 maunds and 39.4 kilograms per acre, followed by Mr. Shafiq Ahmed from Attock with 69 maunds and 39.1 kilograms per acre. Mr. Muhammad Asghar from Rahim Yar Khan secured third position with 69 maunds and 24.1 kilograms per acre.

As part of the prize distribution, three tractors were awarded to the provincial winners. At the district level, Honda CD 70 motorcycles and LED TVs were presented to all district level positions. Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research, Mr. Rana Tanveer Hussain, addressed the ceremony virtually and said, “I congratulate Fatima Fertilizer and all the farmers using Sarsabz fertilisers on securing all three provincial titles and 119 out of 120 district-level positions in the Punjab Wheat Yield Competition. This remarkable achievement is a source of pride for Pakistan. Increasing wheat production and improving crop yields are essential for strengthening Pakistan’s food security. The government is committed to ensuring the procurement of every grain of wheat in coordination with provincial governments. We are also introducing initiatives to improve farmers’ access to quality seeds, modern technology and agricultural financing.

I appreciate Fatima Fertilizer’s efforts in promoting balanced fertiliser use and providing farmers with modern agricultural knowledge and advisory services. The government, private sector, research institutions and farmers must work together to transform agricultural productivity and achieve national food security.” Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Punjab, Mr. Iftikhar Ali Sahoo said that farmers are the backbone of Pakistan’s economy and food security, adding that the government is committed to supporting them through farmer-friendly policies and timely agricultural initiatives. He appreciated Fatima Fertilizer for recognising Punjab’s leading wheat growers and encouraging excellence in agriculture. He said the announced wheat support price of Rs 4,500 per maund, alongside Rs 150 billion in interest-free loans extended to one million farmers through the Kissan Card since October 15, would help farmers access quality seeds and fertilisers on time and strengthen wheat production.

Speaking at the event, Director Marketing and Sales at Fatima Fertilizer, Ms. Rabel Sadozai said, “Last year (2024-25), Sarsabz users also claimed all three provincial positions and 97 of 120 district positions. This year’s results reflect an improvement on last year and highlight the potential to improve wheat produce through balanced crop nutrition and agronomic guidance. Through Sarsabz, we encourage informed farming practices that help farmers make every acre count, strengthen their livelihoods and contribute to Pakistan’s food security.”

The results also highlight the potential to achieve nearly two acres’ worth of national wheat yield from a single acre. While successful Sarsabz farmers recorded yields of approximately 69-70 maunds per acre, the indicative national average stood at around 33 maunds per acre, thus doubling their yield. Fatima Fertilizer supports farmers through agricultural advisory services and soil testing facilities, helping them make informed decisions about their land’s nutritional requirements.” Through its Sarsabz range, including Nitrophos and CAN, Fatima Fertilizer continues to promote balanced crop nutrition and improved farming practices to help farmers increase productivity and contribute to the country’s food security.

headline: PM Shehbaz calls for stronger political engagement to deepen Pakistan-China ties
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has stressed the importance of regular political engagement and exchanges between political parties to further strengthen
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has stressed the importance of regular political engagement and exchanges between political parties to further strengthen relations between Pakistan and China, describing their partnership as ironclad, time-tested and all-weather.

He made these remarks during a meeting with Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC), who visited the prime minister along with a delegation, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office.

Welcoming the Chinese official and his delegation, Shehbaz said the friendship between the two countries was built on mutual trust, respect and strong people-to-people ties.

He acknowledged the IDCPC’s contribution to strengthening institutional connections and encouraging cooperation between the political leadership of Pakistan and China.

Reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to close cooperation with Beijing, the prime minister highlighted several areas where both countries could further expand their partnership, including trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure, information technology and the modernisation of agriculture.

He said sustained engagement at the political level and stronger institutional cooperation were vital to taking the longstanding strategic relationship forward.

Liu Haixing conveyed greetings from the Chinese leadership to the prime minister and reaffirmed Beijing’s resolve to further strengthen its longstanding friendship with Pakistan.

He also welcomed the growing momentum in high-level contacts and exchanges between the political parties of the two countries, saying these efforts would help strengthen bilateral relations.

The two sides also discussed regional and international developments and agreed to maintain close coordination and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral forums.

Later, the prime minister hosted a banquet in honour of Liu Haixing and the visiting delegation.

Welcoming the Chinese official and his delegation, Shehbaz said the friendship between the two countries was built on mutual trust, respect and strong people-to-people ties.

He said sustained engagement at the political level and stronger institutional cooperation were vital to taking the longstanding strategic relationship forward.

headline: Petrol price cut by Rs3.40 per litre, diesel by Rs7.76
description: The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) on Monday announced a Rs3.40 per litre cut in petrol prices and a Rs7.76 per litre cut in high-speed diesel (HSD)
author: APP
article_text:
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) on Monday announced a Rs3.40 per litre cut in petrol prices and a Rs7.76 per litre cut in high-speed diesel (HSD) prices.

According to a press release issued by OGRA, the ex-depot price of petrol (motor spirit) has been reduced from Rs377.91 to Rs374.51 per litre.

Similarly, the price of high-speed diesel has been cut from Rs402.96 to Rs395.20 per litre.

The revised prices will take effect from November 3, 2026.

The new prices have been determined in accordance with the petroleum products pricing mechanism issued by the federal government.

headline: Salman Safdar meets Imran Khan after seven months; PTI forms committee on jail access
description: Lawyer Salman Safdar met Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi in jail, with the meeting lasting around 40 minutes,
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lawyer Salman Safdar met Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi in jail, with the meeting lasting around 40 minutes, according to details shared after the visit.

The meeting began at 4:30 pm and marked Safdar’s first meeting with Imran Khan in seven months, despite repeated requests for access. He also met Bushra Bibi for the first time in 11 months.

Safdar said the brief meeting did not provide enough time to discuss all the cases and legal matters involving the PTI founder.

During the meeting, Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi updated the lawyer on their health and conditions inside the prison. They also gave him fresh instructions concerning their pending cases and other legal matters.

Meanwhile, sources said the PTI parliamentary party had decided to extend conditional support to the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment, linking its backing to Imran Khan’s release.

According to the sources, most participants favoured making the party’s support for the proposed amendment conditional on the PTI founder’s release.

The parliamentary party also decided to establish a six-member steering committee to address concerns over access to Imran Khan and arrangements for his medical treatment.

Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas will lead the committee. It will also include two members of the National Assembly, two senators and representatives from Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The committee will engage with the government and other relevant stakeholders to discuss these matters, sources added.

headline: ECP says 1,847 nomination papers issued for Islamabad LG polls over weekend
description: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has rejected reports that nomination papers for the upcoming Islamabad local government elections were not issued
author: APP
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has rejected reports that nomination papers for the upcoming Islamabad local government elections were not issued over the weekend, saying 16 Returning Officers (ROs) distributed 1,847 forms between October 30 and November 1.

In a clarification issued on Monday, the ECP spokesperson said the reports followed claims made by a political office bearer during an interview with a private news channel. The individual had alleged that nomination papers were unavailable from Friday to Sunday because the Returning Officers’ offices remained closed.

The spokesperson described the claims as misleading and inconsistent with official records, warning that such statements could cause confusion among voters and potential candidates.

According to the ECP's records, all relevant RO offices remained open throughout the three-day period, with 16 Returning Officers issuing a combined total of 1,847 nomination papers.

The commission urged the public and prospective candidates to obtain election-related information only from verified official sources.

It also clarified that candidates could collect and submit their nomination papers at the offices of their respective Returning Officers until November 6.

headline: Direct flights imperative to give quantum jump to Pak-Spanish bilateral trade: Carlos Aragon
description: Ambassador of Spain to Pakistan Carlos Aragon said that Pakistan and Spain should seriously concentrate on starting direct flights between the two countries,
author: APP
article_text: Ambassador of Spain to Pakistan Carlos Aragon said that Pakistan and Spain should seriously concentrate on starting direct flights between the two countries, as it is imperative to give a quantum jump to bilateral trade. Addressing the business community at the Faisalabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry (FCCI), he said that the visa processing would be streamlined to ensure visas for the business community without any unnecessary delay on a top-priority basis. He said that women empowerment, minimizing the impacts of climate change, and promotion of the circular economy are the top priorities of the Spanish government, and there were chances for collaboration with Pakistan in these fields. He said that Spain was making efforts to enhance women's empowerment in collaboration with the UN, while a UNICEF-funded project has been launched in Punjab to equip young girls with training and skills. He was optimistic that its first phase would be completed by the end of the current year, while the second phase would be started after its culmination. About the circular economy, Mr. Carlos said that Spain has a national-level strategy which was introduced 4-5 years ago. He said that we do not have any formal agreement with Pakistan in this respect, but some Spanish companies are exporting textile recycling machinery to Pakistan. About education, he said that Spanish universities are offering the best opportunities to Pakistani students to groom and grow. He further said that Pakistani alumni of Spanish universities could play a positive role in promoting the soft image of their country at the global level. He assured that the Spanish embassy will cooperate to further strengthen the relations between the Pakistani students and Spanish universities. He was optimistic that our bilateral relations could further grow through air connectivity, visa facilitation, women empowerment, circular economy, textile recycling and higher education. We could also help Pakistan in the promotion of the renewable energy sector, he added. Earlier in his welcome address, Mr. Arif Ehsan Malik, President FCCI, said that there was huge untapped potential for the promotion of bilateral trade between Pakistan and Spain. He invited Spanish investors to invest in M3 Industrial Estate and said that he was trying to declare Faisalabad as the first circular city of Pakistan, as it was consuming 90% of textile and 65% of plastic waste. He said that FCCI is an elected platform of the business community of Faisalabad. “It has 20,000 members and is regarded as the textile engine of Pakistan”, he said and thanked Mr. Carlos for giving GSP Plus status to Pakistan. He said that most of the exporters are fully complying with the labor, environment laws in addition to fulfilling their other global responsibilities. He said that Pakistan is providing traditional textile products which could be co-branded in collaboration with Spanish counterparts. He appreciated the Spanish expertise in the production of olive oil and said that we could also collaborate in this field for the benefit of the two countries. He floated a proposal for collaboration between the Spanish design school and the Textile University of Faisalabad for the promotion of industrial design, fashion, and new innovations. A question-and-answer session was held, which was attended by Mr. Kashif Zia, Muhammad Faheem, Madam Kanwal Saeed, Dr. Muzamil Hussain, Hunain Hamid, Muhammad Umer, Mudassar Amin, Taimoor Tahir, Muhammad Awais, Muhammad Yousaf and Sohail Butt. Later, Senior Vice President of FCCI, Mian Muhammad Saeed, offered a vote of thanks, while President Arif Ehsan Malik presented the FCCI shield to Mr. Carlos Aragon, Ambassador of Spain.

He was optimistic that our bilateral relations could further grow through air connectivity, visa facilitation, women empowerment, circular economy, textile recycling and higher education.

We could also help Pakistan in the promotion of the renewable energy sector, he added.

Earlier in his welcome address, Mr. Arif Ehsan Malik, President FCCI, said that there was huge untapped potential for the promotion of bilateral trade between Pakistan and Spain.

He invited Spanish investors to invest in M3 Industrial Estate and said that he was trying to declare Faisalabad as the first circular city of Pakistan, as it was consuming 90% of textile and 65% of plastic waste.

He said that FCCI is an elected platform of the business community of Faisalabad. “It has 20,000 members and is regarded as the textile engine of Pakistan”, he said and thanked Mr. Carlos for giving GSP Plus status to Pakistan.

He said that most of the exporters are fully complying with the labor, environment laws in addition to fulfilling their other global responsibilities.

He said that Pakistan is providing traditional textile products which could be co-branded in collaboration with Spanish counterparts.

He appreciated the Spanish expertise in the production of olive oil and said that we could also collaborate in this field for the benefit of the two countries.

He floated a proposal for collaboration between the Spanish design school and the Textile University of Faisalabad for the promotion of industrial design, fashion, and new innovations.

A question-and-answer session was held, which was attended by Mr. Kashif Zia, Muhammad Faheem, Madam Kanwal Saeed, Dr. Muzamil Hussain, Hunain Hamid, Muhammad Umer, Mudassar Amin, Taimoor Tahir, Muhammad Awais, Muhammad Yousaf and Sohail Butt.

Later, Senior Vice President of FCCI, Mian Muhammad Saeed, offered a vote of thanks, while President Arif Ehsan Malik presented the FCCI shield to Mr. Carlos Aragon, Ambassador of Spain.

headline: Al-Shifa Trust to organize free eye surgical camp
description: Al-Shifa Centre for Community Ophthalmology (ACCO) is organizing a free eye surgical camp at Tehsil Headquarters (THQ) Hospital Ghazi, Haripur, on November 3-4
author: APP
article_text:
Al-Shifa Centre for Community Ophthalmology (ACCO) is organizing a free eye surgical camp at Tehsil Headquarters (THQ) Hospital, Ghazi, Haripur, on November 3-4 to provide eye care services to residents at their doorstep.

The camp will operate from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., offering an opportunity for local residents to access free eye care and surgical services.

The initiative aims to facilitate people, particularly those facing difficulties in travelling to major healthcare facilities, by bringing specialized eye care services closer to their communities.

Al-Shifa Trust has also invited public support for its community eye care initiatives.
